٦١٧٥ — عن ابن مسعود قال:

أوتي رسول الله ﷺ جوامع الخير وخواتمه، أو قال: فواتح الخير، فعلّمنا خطبة الصلاة وخطبة الحاجة.

خطبة الصلاة:

«التَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ، وَالصَّلَوَاتُ وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ».

وخطبة الحاجة:

«إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ لِلَّهِ، نَحْمَدُهُ وَنَسْتَعِينُهُ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهُ، وَنَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شُرُورِ أَنْفُسِنَا وَمِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ أَعْمَالِنَا، مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهُ، وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ».

ثم تصل خطبتك بثلاث آيات من كتاب الله:

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾

 [آل عمران: ١٠٢]

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالْأَرْحَامَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا﴾

 [النساء: ١]

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا ۝ يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ فَازَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا﴾

 [الأحزاب: ٧٠-٧١]

صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢١١٨)، والترمذي (١١٠٥) وحسنه، والنسائي (٣٢٧٧)، وابن ماجه (١٨٩٢).

6175 — Ibn Masʿūd reported:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was given comprehensive expressions of goodness and their conclusions—or he said, their beginnings. He taught us the tashahhud of prayer and the sermon of need.

The tashahhud of prayer is:

“All greetings are for Allah, as are the prayers and all good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.”

The sermon of need is:

“Indeed, all praise belongs to Allah. We praise Him, seek His help, and seek His forgiveness. We seek refuge in Allah from the evils within ourselves and from our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can misguide; and whomever He leaves astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god except Allah alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.”

Then connect your sermon with three verses from the Book of Allah:

“O you who believe, fear Allah as He should truly be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.”

 [Āl ʿImrān: 102]

“O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from a single soul, and created from it its mate, and spread from the two many men and women. And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the ties of kinship. Indeed, Allah is ever Watchful over you.”

 [al-Nisāʾ: 1]

“O you who believe, fear Allah and speak words that are right. He will set right your deeds for you and forgive your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great triumph.”

 [al-Aḥzāb: 70–71]

Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (2118), al-Tirmidhī (1105), who graded it Hasan, al-Nasāʾī (3277), and Ibn Mājah (1892).

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾

 [آل عمران: ١٠٢]

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالْأَرْحَامَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا﴾

 [النساء: ١]

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا ۝ يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ فَازَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا﴾

 [الأحزاب: ٧٠-٧١]

صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢١١٨)، والترمذي (١١٠٥) وحسنه، والنسائي (٣٢٧٧)، وابن ماجه (١٨٩٢). 

6175 — Ibn Masʿūd reported:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was given comprehensive expressions of goodness and their conclusions—or he said, their beginnings. He taught us the tashahhud of prayer and the sermon of need.

The tashahhud of prayer is:

“All greetings are for Allah, as are the prayers and all good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.”

The sermon of need is:

“Indeed, all praise belongs to Allah. We praise Him, seek His help, and seek His forgiveness. We seek refuge in Allah from the evils within ourselves and from our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can misguide; and whomever He leaves astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god except Allah alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.”

Then connect your sermon with three verses from the Book of Allah:

“O you who believe, fear Allah as He should truly be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.”

 [Āl ʿImrān: 102]

“O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from a single soul, and created from it its mate, and spread from the two many men and women. And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the ties of kinship. Indeed, Allah is ever Watchful over you.”

 [al-Nisāʾ: 1]

“O you who believe, fear Allah and speak words that are right. He will set right your deeds for you and forgive your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great triumph.”

 [al-Aḥzāb: 70–71]

Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (2118), al-Tirmidhī (1105), who graded it Hasan, al-Nasāʾī (3277), and Ibn Mājah (1892).

6176 — Abu Hurayrah reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “Every sermon in which there is no declaration of faith is like a severed hand.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (4841), al-Tirmidhi (1118), Ahmad (8018), and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (2796).

“Severed” means cut off, meaning a hand from which no benefit is taken.

٦١٧٧ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: جاء ثلاثة رهط إلى بيوت أزواج النبي ﷺ يسألون عن عبادة النبي ﷺ، فلما أخبروا كأنهم تقالّوها، فقالوا: وأين نحن من النبي ﷺ؟ قد غفر الله له ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر. قال أحدهم: أما أنا فأصلي الليل أبدا. وقال آخر: وأنا أصوم الدهر ولا أفطر. وقال آخر: أنا أعتزل النساء فلا أتزوج أبدا. فجاء رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: (( أنتم الذين قلتم كذا وكذا؟ أما والله إني لأخشاكم لله وأتقاكم له، لكني أصوم وأفطر، وأصلي وأرقد، وأتزوج النساء، فمن رغب عن سنتي فليس مني )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٠٦٣)، ومسلم (١٤٠١).

english_source:
6177 — Anas ibn Malik said: Three men came to the houses of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ asking about the worship of the Prophet ﷺ. When they were informed, they seemed to think it little. They said: Where are we compared to the Prophet ﷺ, when Allah has forgiven his past and future sins? One of them said: As for me, I will pray all night forever. Another said: I will fast continuously and never break my fast. Another said: I will keep away from women and never marry. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and said: “Are you the ones who said such and such? By Allah, I am the one among you who fears Allah most and is most mindful of Him, but I fast and I break the fast, I pray and I sleep, and I marry women. So whoever turns away from my way is not of me.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5063) and Muslim (1401).

٦١٧٨ — عن سعيد بن جبير قال: قال لي ابن عباس: هل تزوجت؟ قلت: لا. قال: فتزوج؛ فإن خير هذه الأمة أكثرها نساء.

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥٠٦٩).

6178 — Sa‘id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn ‘Abbas said to me: Have you married? I said: No. He said: Then marry, for the best of this community were those who had the most wives.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5069).

arabic_source:
٦١٧٩ — عن علقمة قال: كنت أمشي مع عبد الله بمنى، فلقيه عثمان، فقام معه يحدثه. فقال له عثمان: يا أبا عبد الرحمن، ألا نزوجك جارية شابة لعلها تذكرك بعض ما مضى من زمانك. قال: فقال عبد الله: لئن قلت ذاك، لقد قال لنا رسول الله ﷺ: (( يا معشر الشباب، من استطاع منكم الباءة فليتزوج، فإنه أغض للبصر، وأحصن للفرج، ومن لم يستطع فعليه بالصوم، فإنه له وجاء )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٠٦٥)، ومسلم (١:١٤٠٠). واللفظ لمسلم.

والباءة معناها الجماع، وأصلها المكان الذي يأوي إليه الإنسان، وسمي النكاح بها؛ لأن من تزوج امرأة بوأها منزلا. (( شرح السنة )) (٤/٩)

english_source:
6179 — ‘Alqamah said: I was walking with ‘Abd Allah at Mina when ‘Uthman met him and stood speaking with him. ‘Uthman said to him: O Abu ‘Abd al-Rahman, shall we not marry you to a young woman? Perhaps she may remind you of some of what has passed from your earlier days. ‘Abd Allah said: If you say that, then indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: “O company of young men, whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry, for it is more effective in lowering the gaze and better in guarding chastity. And whoever is not able, then he should fast, for it is a restraint for him.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5065) and Muslim (1400:1). The wording here is that of Muslim.

The word used here means sexual ability. Originally it refers to the place where a person resides, and marriage was called by this term because whoever marries a woman settles her in a home. (Sharh al-Sunnah, 4/9)

٦١٧٩ — عن علقمة قال: كنت أمشي مع عبد الله بمنى، فلقيه عثمان، فقام معه يحدثه. فقال له عثمان: يا أبا عبد الرحمن، ألا نزوجك جارية شابة لعلها تذكرك بعض ما مضى من زمانك. قال: فقال عبد الله: لئن قلت ذاك، لقد قال لنا رسول الله ﷺ: (( يا معشر الشباب، من استطاع منكم الباءة فليتزوج، فإنه أغض للبصر، وأحصن للفرج، ومن لم يستطع فعليه بالصوم، فإنه له وجاء )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٠٦٥)، ومسلم (١:١٤٠٠). واللفظ لمسلم.

والباءة معناها الجماع، وأصلها المكان الذي يأوي إليه الإنسان، وسمي النكاح بها؛ لأن من تزوج امرأة بوأها منزلا. (( شرح السنة )) (٤/٩)

6179 — ‘Alqamah said: I was walking with ‘Abd Allah at Mina when ‘Uthman met him and stood speaking with him. ‘Uthman said to him: O Abu ‘Abd al-Rahman, shall we not marry you to a young woman? Perhaps she may remind you of some of what has passed from your earlier days. ‘Abd Allah said: If you say that, then indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: “O company of young men, whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry, for it is more effective in lowering the gaze and better in guarding chastity. And whoever is not able, then he should fast, for it is a restraint for him.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5065) and Muslim (1400:1). The wording here is that of Muslim.

The word used here means sexual ability. Originally it refers to the place where a person resides, and marriage was called by this term because whoever marries a woman settles her in a home. (Sharh al-Sunnah, 4/9)

٦١٨١ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: كنا نغزو مع رسول الله ﷺ وليس لنا شيء، فقلنا: ألا نستخصي؟ فنهانا عن ذلك، ثم رخص لنا أن ننكح المرأة بالثوب، ثم قرأ علينا: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُحَرِّمُوا طَيِّبَاتِ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَلَا تَعْتَدُوا ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ) [المائدة: ٨٧]

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٠٧٥)، ومسلم (١٤٠٤). واللفظ للبخاري.

٦١٨٣ — عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال: لما كان من أمر عثمان بن مظعون الذي كان من ترك النساء بعث إليه رسول الله ﷺ فقال: (( يا عثمان، إني لم أؤمر بالرهبانية، أرغبت عن سنتي؟ )) قال: لا، يا رسول الله. قال: (( إن من سنتي أن أصلي وأنام، وأصوم وأطعم، وأنكح وأطلق، فمن رغب عن سنتي فليس مني، يا عثمان، إن لأهلك عليك حقا، ولنفسك عليك حقا )).

قال سعد: فوالله لقد كان أجمع رجال من المسلمين على أن رسول الله ﷺ إن هو أقر عثمان على ما هو عليه أن نختصي فنتبتل.

حسن: رواه الدارمي (٢٢١٥).

قوله: (( التبتل )) أصله القطع. والمراد الانقطاع عن النساء وترك النكاح انقطاعا إلى عبادة الله.

قوله: (( لاختصينا )) الخصاء هو نزع البيضتين من الخصيتين بشق جلدها.

english_source:
6183 — Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas said: When the matter of ‘Uthman ibn Maz‘un occurred regarding his leaving women aside, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for him and said: “O ‘Uthman, I was not commanded with monasticism. Have you turned away from my way?” He said: No, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “Part of my way is that I pray and I sleep, I fast and I eat, and I marry and divorce. Whoever turns away from my way is not of me. O ‘Uthman, your family has a right over you, and your own self has a right over you.”

Sa‘d said: By Allah, the Muslim men were on the verge of agreeing that if the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had approved ‘Uthman in what he was doing, we would have castrated ourselves and lived in celibacy.

Hasan: Narrated by al-Darimi (2215).

His statement, “celibacy,” originally means cutting off. What is meant is cutting oneself off from women and leaving marriage in order to devote oneself entirely to worship of Allah.

His statement, “we would have castrated ourselves,” means removing the two testicles by cutting the skin covering them.

٦١٨٤ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قلت يا رسول الله ﷺ إني رجل شاب، وأنا أخاف على نفسي العنت ولا أجد ما أتزوج به النساء، فسكت عني، ثم قلت مثل ذلك، فسكت عني، ثم قلت له مثل ذلك، فسكت عني. ثم قلت مثل ذلك. فقال النبي ﷺ: (( يا أبا هريرة، جف القلم بما أنت لاق، فاختص على ذلك أو ذر )).

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥٠٧٦).

6184 — Abu Hurayrah said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, I am a young man, and I fear hardship for myself, and I do not find what I can marry women with. He remained silent toward me. Then I said the same again, and he remained silent. Then I said it again, and he remained silent. Then I said it again, so the Prophet ﷺ said: “O Abu Hurayrah, the pen has dried regarding what you are going to meet, so castrate yourself on that basis or leave it.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5076).

٦١٨٤ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قلت يا رسول الله ﷺ إني رجل شاب، وأنا أخاف على نفسي العنت ولا أجد ما أتزوج به النساء، فسكت عني، ثم قلت مثل ذلك، فسكت عني، ثم قلت له مثل ذلك، فسكت عني. ثم قلت مثل ذلك. فقال النبي ﷺ: (( يا أبا هريرة، جف القلم بما أنت لاق، فاختص على ذلك أو ذر )).

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥٠٧٦).

٦١٩٠ — عن عائشة قالت: دخلت امرأة عثمان بن مظعون واسمها خولة بنت حكيم على عائشة وهي باذة الهيئة، فسألتها ما شأنك؟ فقالت: زوجي يقوم الليل، ويصوم النهار. فدخل النبي ﷺ فذكرت ذلك له عائشة. فلقي النبي ﷺ فقال: (( يا عثمان، إن الرهبانية لم تكتب علينا، أما لك في أسوة؟ فوالله إن أخشاكم لله، وأحفظكم لحدوده لأنا )).

صحيح: رواه عبد الرزاق (١٠٣٧٥)، والبزار - كشف الأستار (١٤٥٨)، وابن حبان (٩).

english_source:
6190 — ‘A’ishah said: The wife of ‘Uthman ibn Maz‘un, whose name was Khawlah bint Hakim, came to ‘A’ishah while she was in poor appearance. She asked her: What is the matter with you? She said: My husband stands in prayer all night and fasts all day. Then the Prophet ﷺ came in, and ‘A’ishah mentioned that to him. So the Prophet ﷺ met ‘Uthman and said: “O ‘Uthman, monasticism has not been prescribed for us. Do you not have an example in me? By Allah, I am the one among you who fears Allah most and guards His limits best.”

Authentic: Narrated by ‘Abd al-Razzaq (10375), al-Bazzar in Kashf al-Astar (1458), and Ibn Hibban (9).

arabic_source:
٦١٩١ — عن عائشة قالت: كانت امرأة عثمان بن مظعون تختضب وتطيب، فتركته، فدخلت علي، فقلت لها: أمشهد أم مغيب؟ فقالت: مشهد كمغيب. قلت لها: مالك؟ قالت: عثمان لا يريد الدنيا، ولا يريد النساء. قالت عائشة: فدخل علي رسول الله ﷺ فأخبرته بذلك. فلقي عثمان فقال: (( يا عثمان، أتؤمن بما نؤمن به؟ )) قال: نعم يا رسول الله. قال: (( فاصنع كما نصنع )).

حسن: رواه الإمام أحمد (٢٤٧٥٤)، وأبو نعيم في الحلية (٦/٢٥٧).

٦١٩١ — عن عائشة قالت: كانت امرأة عثمان بن مظعون تختضب وتطيب، فتركته، فدخلت علي، فقلت لها: أمشهد أم مغيب؟ فقالت: مشهد كمغيب. قلت لها: مالك؟ قالت: عثمان لا يريد الدنيا، ولا يريد النساء. قالت عائشة: فدخل علي رسول الله ﷺ فأخبرته بذلك. فلقي عثمان فقال: (( يا عثمان، أتؤمن بما نؤمن به؟ )) قال: نعم يا رسول الله. قال: (( فاصنع كما نصنع )).

حسن: رواه الإمام أحمد (٢٤٧٥٤)، وأبو نعيم في الحلية (٦/٢٥٧).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٧٢١)، ومسلم (١٤١٨).

٦١٩٣ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: (( ثلاثة كلهم حق على الله عونه: الغازي في سبيل الله، والمكاتب الذي يريد الأداء، والناكح الذي يريد التعفف )).

حسن: رواه الترمذي (١٦٥٥) وحسّنه، والنسائي (٣٢١٨، ٣١٢٠)، وابن ماجه (٢٥١٨)، وأحمد (٧٤١٦).

6193 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Three people all have a right upon Allah that He help them: the fighter in the path of Allah, the contracted slave who wants to complete his payment, and the one who marries seeking chastity.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (1655), who graded it Hasan, al-Nasa’i (3218, 3120), Ibn Majah (2518), and Ahmad (7416).

٦١٩٤ — عن جابر بن عبد الله، أن النبي ﷺ قال: (( إذا دخلت ليلا، فلا تدخل على أهلك حتى تستحد المغيبة، وتمتشط الشعثة )). قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: (( فعليك بالكيس الكيس )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٢٤٦)، ومسلم (٥٧:٧١٥).

قوله: (( فعليك بالكيس الكيس )) فسره البخاري في الحديث الذي قبله بالولد، يعني طلب الولد. وقال ابن الأعرابي: الكيس: الجماع. والكيس: العقل، والمراد حثه على ابتغاء الولد. انظر: شرح مسلم للنووي (١٠/٥٤).

6194 — Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “If you arrive at night, do not enter upon your family until the woman whose husband was absent removes her unwanted hair and the disheveled woman combs her hair.” Jabir said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “So hold fast to good sense, hold fast to good sense.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5246) and Muslim (715:57).

His statement, “So hold fast to good sense,” was explained by al-Bukhari in the preceding narration as referring to children, meaning seeking offspring. Ibn al-A‘rabi said: the word can mean intercourse. It also means intelligence. What is meant here is encouraging him to seek children. See Sharh Muslim by al-Nawawi (10/54).

٦١٩٥ — عن معقل بن يسار قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي ﷺ فقال: إني أصبت امرأة ذات حسب وجمال، إلا أنها لا تلد، أفأتزوجها؟ قال: (( لا )). ثم أتاه الثانية، فنهاه، ثم أتاه الثالثة، فقال: (( تزوجوا الودود الولود، فإني مكاثر بكم )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٠٥٠)، والنسائي (٣٢٢٧).

6195 — Ma‘qil ibn Yasar said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “I have found a woman of noble lineage and beauty, but she does not bear children. Should I marry her?” He said, “No.” Then he came to him a second time, and he forbade him. Then he came a third time, and he said, “Marry the loving, fertile women, for I will boast of your numbers.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2050) and al-Nasa’i (3227).

٦١٩٦ — عن ابن عمر أنه تزوج امرأة فأصابها شمطاء فطلقها، وقال: حصير في بيت خير من امرأة لا تلد. والله ما أقربكن شهوة، ولكني سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: (( تزوجوا الودود الولود، فإني مكاثر بكم الأمم يوم القيامة )).

صحيح: رواه الخطيب في تاريخ بغداد (٦٧٨٢).

english_source:
6196 — Ibn ‘Umar reported that he married a woman, then found her gray-haired, so he divorced her. He said:

“A mat in the house is better than a woman who does not bear children. By Allah, it is not desire for women that brings me near to you, but I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: ‘Marry the loving, fertile women, for I will boast of your numbers before the nations on the Day of Resurrection.’”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad (6782).

صحيح: رواه الخطيب في تاريخ بغداد (٦٧٨٢).

6196 — Ibn ‘Umar reported that he married a woman, then found her gray-haired, so he divorced her. He said:

“A mat in the house is better than a woman who does not bear children. By Allah, it is not desire for women that brings me near to you, but I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: ‘Marry the loving, fertile women, for I will boast of your numbers before the nations on the Day of Resurrection.’”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad (6782).

٦١٩٧ — عن جابر بن عبد الله قال:

قفلنا مع النبي ﷺ من غزوة، فتعجلت على بعير لي قطوف، فلحقني راكب من خلفي، فنخس بعيري بعنزة كانت معه، فانطلق بعيري كأجود ما أنت راء من الإبل.

فإذا النبي ﷺ، فقال:

«مَا يُعْجِلُكَ؟»

قلت: كنت حديث عهد بعرس.

قال:

«أَبِكْرًا أَمْ ثَيِّبًا؟»

قلت: ثيبًا.

قال:

«فَهَلَّا جَارِيَةً تُلَاعِبُهَا وَتُلَاعِبُكَ؟»

قال: فلما ذهبنا لندخل قال:

«أَمْهِلُوا حَتَّى تَدْخُلُوا لَيْلًا - أَيْ عِشَاءً - لِكَيْ تَمْتَشِطَ الشَّعِثَةُ، وَتَسْتَحِدَّ الْمُغِيبَةُ».

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٠٧٩)، ومسلم (٧١٥/٥٧). 

قوله: «قطوف» أي بطيء المشي.

وقوله: «الشعثة» هي المرأة المتفرقة شعر الرأس، أي لتتزين هي لزوجها.

6197 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh reported:

We were returning with the Prophet ﷺ from an expedition. I hurried ahead on a camel of mine that was slow in walking. A rider caught up with me from behind and prodded my camel with a stick that he had, whereupon my camel began moving as well as the best camel you could see.

It was the Prophet ﷺ. He asked:

“What is making you hurry?”

I replied:

“I have recently been married.”

He asked:

“A virgin or a previously married woman?”

I replied:

“A previously married woman.”

He said:

“Why not a young virgin whom you could play with and who could play with you?”

When we were about to enter Madinah, he said:

“Wait until you enter at night—that is, in the evening—so that the woman whose hair is disheveled may comb it, and the woman whose husband has been absent may remove her unwanted hair.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5079) and Muslim (715/57). 

“Qaṭūf” means slow in walking.

“Al-shaʿithah” means a woman whose hair is disordered, so that she may beautify herself for her husband.

٦١٩٨ — عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: هلك أبي وترك سبع بنات، أو تسع بنات، فتزوجت امرأة ثيباً، فقال لي رسول الله ﷺ: (( تزوجت يا جابر؟ )) فقلت: نعم. فقال: (( بكراً أم ثيباً؟ )) قلت: بل ثيباً. قال: (( فهلا جارية تلاعبها وتلاعبك، وتضاحكها وتضاحكك؟ )) قال: فقلت له: إن عبد الله هلك وترك بنات، وإني كرهت أن أجيئهن بمثلهن، فتزوجت امرأة تقوم عليهن وتصلحهن. فقال: (( بارك الله لك - أو قال: خيراً )).

وفي لفظ: فكرهت أن أجمع إليهن جارية خرقاء مثلهن، ولكن امرأة تمشطهن وتقوم عليهن.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٣٦٧)، ومسلم (٥٦:٧١٥). واللفظ الآخر للبخاري في المغازي (٤٠٥٢).

6198 — Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah said: My father died and left behind seven daughters, or nine daughters, so I married a previously married woman. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me, “Have you married, O Jabir?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “A virgin or a previously married woman?” I said, “Rather, a previously married woman.” He said, “Why not a young virgin, so that you may play with her and she may play with you, and make her laugh and she make you laugh?”

He said: I said to him, “ ‘Abd Allah died and left daughters, and I disliked bringing them someone like themselves, so I married a woman who would look after them and set their affairs right.” He said, “May Allah bless you,” or he said, “Good.”

And in another wording: “I disliked bringing together with them a young inexperienced girl like them; rather I wanted a woman who would comb their hair and take care of them.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5367) and Muslim (715:56). The alternate wording is in al-Bukhari in the Book of Military Expeditions (4052).

6199 — Jabir said: I married a woman, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me, “Have you married?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “A virgin or a previously married woman?” I said, “A previously married woman.” He said, “Then where are you with young virgins and their playfulness?”

Shu‘bah said: I mentioned this to ‘Amr ibn Dinar, and he said: I heard it from Jabir, and he only said: “Why not a young girl that you may play with her and she may play with you?”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5080) and Muslim (715:55). The wording here is that of Muslim.

٦٢٠٣ — عن جابر قال: تزوجت امرأة في عهد رسول الله ﷺ فلقيت النبي ﷺ فقال: (( يا جابر تزوجت؟ )) قلت: نعم. قال: (( بكر أم ثيب؟ )) قلت: ثيب. قال: (( فهلا بكراً تلاعبها؟ )) قلت: يا رسول الله، إن لي أخوات فخشيت أن تدخل بيني وبينهن. قال: (( فذاك إذن، إن المرأة تنكح على دينها، ومالها، وجمالها، فعليك بذات الدين تربت يداك )).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٥٤:٧١٥).

٦٢٠٦ — عن سهل بن سعد، قال: مر رجل على رسول الله ﷺ فقال: (( ما تقولون في هذا؟ )) قالوا: حري إن خطب أن ينكح، وإن شفع أن يشفع، وإن قال أن يستمع. قال: ثم سكت. فمر رجل من فقراء المسلمين، فقال: (( ما تقولون في هذا؟ )) قالوا: حري إن خطب أن لا ينكح، وإن شفع أن لا يشفع، وإن قال أن لا يستمع. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: (( هذا خير من ملء الأرض مثل هذا )).

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥٠٩١).

6206 — Sahl ibn Sa‘d said: A man passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said, “What do you say about this one?” They said: He is deserving, if he proposes, to be married to; if he intercedes, to have his intercession accepted; and if he speaks, to be listened to. Then he remained silent. Then a poor man from among the Muslims passed by, and he said, “What do you say about this one?” They said: He is deserving, if he proposes, not to be married to; if he intercedes, not to have his intercession accepted; and if he speaks, not to be listened to. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “This one is better than the whole earth filled with the likes of that one.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5091).

٦٢٠٧ — عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: (( أربع من السعادة: المرأة الصالحة، والمسكن الواسع، والجار الصالح، والمركب الهنيء. وأربع من الشقاوة: الجار السوء، والمرأة السوء، والمسكن الضيق، والمركب السوء )).

Authentic: Narrated by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (4032).

arabic_source:
٦٢٠٨ — عن رجل من أصحاب النبي أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: (( تبا للذهب والفضة )). قال: فانطلقت مع عمر بن الخطاب، فقال: يا رسول الله، قولك: (( تبا للذهب والفضة )) ماذا؟ فقال: (( لساناً ذاكراً، وقلباً شاكراً، زوجة تعين على الآخرة )).

حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٣١٠١).

قوله: (( تباً للذهب والفضة )) أي هلاكاً لمن ادخرهما ولم يؤد زكاتهما.

وقوله: (( ماذا )) أي ماذا نتخذ كما في رواية ثوبان الآتية.

english_source:
6208 — A man from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“Woe to gold and silver.”

He said: So I went with ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he said: O Messenger of Allah, your statement, “Woe to gold and silver” - then what should one have? He said: “A tongue that remembers Allah, a grateful heart, a wife who helps one toward the Hereafter.”

Hasan: Narrated by Ahmad (23101).

His statement, “Woe to gold and silver,” means destruction for the one who hoards them and does not pay their due alms.

His statement, “then what?” means: then what should we acquire, as in the narration of Thawban that comes later.

٦٢٠٩ — عن فاطمة بنت قيس أن أبا عمرو بن حفص طلقها البتة، فذكرت الحديث. قالت: فلما حللت ذكرت للنبي ﷺ أن معاوية بن أبي سفيان، وأبا جهم بن هشام خطباني. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: (( أما أبو جهم فلا يضع عصاه عن عاتقه، وأما معاوية فصعلوك لا مال له، أنكحي أسامة بن زيد )). قالت: فكرهته. ثم قال: (( أنكحي أسامة بن زيد )). فنكحته، فجعل الله في ذلك خيراً، واغتبطت به.

صحيح: رواه مالك (٧٣)، ومسلم (١٤٨٠).

english_source:
6209 — Fatimah bint Qays reported that Abu ‘Amr ibn Hafs divorced her irrevocably. She mentioned the rest of the narration and said: When my waiting period ended, I mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ that Mu‘awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan and Abu Jahm ibn Hisham had proposed to me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “As for Abu Jahm, he does not put down his staff from his shoulder; and as for Mu‘awiyah, he is poor and has no wealth. Marry Usamah ibn Zayd.”

She said: I disliked him. Then he said: “Marry Usamah ibn Zayd.” So I married him, and Allah placed much good in that, and I was pleased with it.

Authentic: Narrated by Malik (73) and Muslim (1480).

٦٢١٠ — عن عائشة أن أبا حذيفة بن عتبة بن ربيعة بن عبد شمس - وكان ممن شهد بدراً مع النبي ﷺ - تبنى سالماً، وأنكحه بنت أخيه - هند بنت الوليد بن عتبة بن ربيعة - وهو مولى لامرأة من الأنصار.

6210 — ‘A’ishah reported that Abu Hudhayfah ibn ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah ibn ‘Abd Shams - and he was among those who witnessed Badr with the Prophet ﷺ - had adopted Salim and married him to the daughter of his brother, Hind bint al-Walid ibn ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah, and he was the freedman of a woman from the Ansar.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5088).

٦٢١٠ — عن عائشة أن أبا حذيفة بن عتبة بن ربيعة بن عبد شمس - وكان ممن شهد بدراً مع النبي ﷺ - تبنى سالماً، وأنكحه بنت أخيه - هند بنت الوليد بن عتبة بن ربيعة - وهو مولى لامرأة من الأنصار.

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥٠٨٨).

6210 — ‘A’ishah reported that Abu Hudhayfah ibn ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah ibn ‘Abd Shams - and he was among those who witnessed Badr with the Prophet ﷺ - had adopted Salim and married him to the daughter of his brother, Hind bint al-Walid ibn ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah, and he was the freedman of a woman from the Ansar.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5088).

٦٢٦٤ — عن عائشة قالت: اختصم سعد بن أبي وقاص وعبد الله بن زمعة في غلام. فقال سعد: هذا يا رسولَ الله ابن أخي عتبة بن أبي وقاص، عَهِد إليَّ أنه ابنه، انظر إلى شبهه. وقال عبد بن زمعة: هذا أخي يا رسول الله، وُلِدَ على فراش أبي من وليدته. فنظر رسول الله ﷺ إلى شبهه، فرأى شبها بيّنا بعتبة، فقال: (( هو لك يا عبد بن زمعة، الولد للفراش، وللعاهر الحجر، واحتجبي منه يا سودة بنت زمعة )). فلم تره قط. وفي رواية زيادة: (( هو أخوك يا عبد )).

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٢٢)، والبخاري (٢٢١٨)، ومسلم (١٤٥٧).

6264 — ‘A’ishah said: Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas and ‘Abdullah ibn Zam‘ah disputed over a boy. Sa‘d said: O Messenger of Allah, this is the son of my brother ‘Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas. He entrusted me that he was his son. Look at his resemblance. ‘Abd ibn Zam‘ah said: This is my brother, O Messenger of Allah. He was born on my father’s bed from his slave-woman. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at his resemblance and saw a clear resemblance to ‘Utbah, so he said: “He is yours, O ‘Abd ibn Zam‘ah. The child belongs to the marriage bed, and the adulterer gets the stone. And veil yourself from him, O Sawdah bint Zam‘ah.” So she never saw him again. In another narration there is the addition: “He is your brother, O ‘Abd.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (22), al-Bukhari (2218), and Muslim (1457).

٦٢٦٥ — عن ابن عمر أن رجلاً من أهل البادية أتى النبي ﷺ فقال: يا رسول الله، إن امرأتي ولدتْ على فراشي غلاماً أسود، وإنا أهل بيت لم يكن فينا أسود قط. قال: (( هل لك من إبل؟ )) قال: نعم. قال: (( فما ألوانها؟ )) قال: حمر. قال: (( هل فيها أسود؟ )) قال: لا. قال: (( فيها أورق؟ )) قال: نعم. قال: (( فأنى كان ذلك؟ )) قال: عسى أن يكون نزعه عرق. قال: (( فلعل ابنك هذا نزعه عِرقٌ )).

حسن: رواه ابن ماجه (٢٠٠٣).

6265 — Ibn ‘Umar narrated that a man from the desert came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, my wife has given birth on my bed to a black boy, and we are a household in which there has never been any black person. He said: “Do you have camels?” He said: Yes. He said: “What are their colors?” He said: Red. He said: “Are there any black among them?” He said: No. He said: “Are there any grayish ones among them?” He said: Yes. He said: “How did that happen?” He said: Perhaps some inherited trait drew it out. He said: “Then perhaps this son of yours was likewise drawn out by an inherited trait.”

Hasan: Narrated by Ibn Majah (2003).

٦٢٧٠ — عن أبي أمامة الباهلي يقول: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول في خطبة عام حجة الوداع: (( الولد للفراش وللعاهر الحجر )).

حسن: رواه الترمذي (٢١٢٠)، وأبو داود (٣٥٦٥)، وابن ماجه (٢٠٠٧)، وأحمد (٢٢٢٩٤).

فقه الباب: كان من عادات الجاهلية إلحاقُ النسب بالزنا، وكانوا يستأجرون الإماء للوَطْءِ، فإن اعترفت الأم بأن الولد له ألحقوه به، فجاء الإسلامُ وأبطلَ ذلك، وأمرَ بإلحاق الولد بالفراش، كما وقع في مخاصمة سعد بن أبي وقاص وعبد بن زمعة بن الأسود في ولدٍ، وذلك أنَّ عتبة بن أبي وقاص وقعَ على أمةِ زمعة بن الأسود، فحملت الأمةُ، وولدتْ غلامًا، فلما حضر وفاةُ عتبة عَهِدَ لأخيه سعد بأن يأخذ هذا الولد، ويلحقه به، ثم مات عتبةُ مشركًا، فحينئذِ تخاصمَ سعدٌ مع عبد بن زمعة في ذلك الغلام، فاحتجَّ سعدٌ لاستلحاق الغلام بأخيه عتبة على عاداتهم في استلحاق الولد بالزنا، وتمسَّكَ عبدُ بنُ زمعة بفراش أبيه، فقضى النبي ﷺ: (( الولدُ للفراشِ ))، وقطعَ الإلحاق بالزنا بقوله: (( وللعاهر الحجرُ )).

6270 — Abu Umamah al-Bahili said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say in the sermon of the Farewell Pilgrimage: “The child belongs to the marriage bed, and the adulterer gets the stone.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2120), Abu Dawud (3565), Ibn Majah (2007), and Ahmad (22294).

Legal understanding of this chapter: It was among the customs of the pre-Islamic period to attach lineage through fornication. They used to hire slave women for intercourse, and if the mother acknowledged that the child belonged to a certain man, they would attach him to him. Islam came and abolished that, and commanded that the child be attributed to the marriage bed. This is what occurred in the dispute between Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas and ‘Abd ibn Zam‘ah ibn al-Aswad over a boy. ‘Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas had intercourse with the slave woman of Zam‘ah ibn al-Aswad, so she became pregnant and gave birth to a boy. When ‘Utbah was on his deathbed, he instructed his brother Sa‘d to take this boy and attribute him to him. ‘Utbah then died as a polytheist. After that, Sa‘d and ‘Abd ibn Zam‘ah disputed about the boy. Sa‘d argued for attributing the boy to his brother ‘Utbah according to their old custom of attributing children through fornication, while ‘Abd ibn Zam‘ah relied on his father’s marriage bed. So the Prophet ﷺ ruled: “The child belongs to the marriage bed,” and cut off attribution through fornication by saying: “and the adulterer gets the stone.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (6770) and Muslim (1459).

٦٢٧١ — عن عائشة قالت: إن رسول الله ﷺ دخل عليّ مسروراً تبرق أسارير وجهه فقال: (( ألم تري أن مجزّزاً نظر آنفا إلى زيد بن حارثة وأسامة بن زيد فقال: إن هذه الأقدام بعضها من بعض )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٧٧٠)، ومسلم (١٤٥٩).

6271 — ‘A’ishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon me happy, with the lines of his face shining, and said: “Did you not see that Mujazziz just now looked at Zayd ibn Harithah and Usamah ibn Zayd and said: These feet belong to one another?”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (6770) and Muslim (1459).

٦٢٧٤ — عن أبي بكر بن أبي الجهم بن صُخير العدوي قال: سمعت فاطمة بنت قيس تقول: إن زوجها طلّقها ثلاثا، فلم يجعل لها رسول الله ﷺ سكنى ولا نفقة، قالت: قال لي رسول الله ﷺ: (( إذا حللتِ فآذنيني )) فآذنته. فخطبها معاوية وأبو جهم وأسامة بن زيد. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: (( أما معاوية فرجل تَرِبٌ لا مال له، وأما أبو جهم فرجل ضرّاب للنساء، ولكن أسامة بن زيد )).

فقالت بيدها هكذا: أسامة! أسامة! فقال لها رسول الله ﷺ: (( طاعة الله وطاعة رسوله خير لك )).

قالت: فتزوجته فاغتبطتُ.

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٤٧:١٤٨٠). وقوله: (( تَرِب )) يعني الفقير، لأنه من شدة فقره يكون ملصقا بالتراب.

english_source:
6274 — Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Jahm ibn Sukhayr al-‘Adawi said: I heard Fatimah bint Qays say that her husband divorced her three times, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not assign for her any housing or maintenance. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me, “When you become lawful for marriage, inform me.” So I informed him. Then Mu‘awiyah, Abu Jahm, and Usamah ibn Zayd proposed to her. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “As for Mu‘awiyah, he is a poor man with no wealth. As for Abu Jahm, he is a man who beats women. Rather, marry Usamah ibn Zayd.”

She gestured with her hand like this and said: Usamah? Usamah? So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: “Obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger are better for you.”

She said: So I married him and was greatly pleased.

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (47:1480). His saying “tārib” means poor, because from the severity of his poverty he is as though attached to the dust.

٦٢٧٥ — عن أبي سلمة، أن فاطمة بنت قيس - أخت الضحاك بن قيس - أخبرته أنّ أبا حفص بن المغيرة المخزومي طلّقها ثلاثاً، ثم انطلق إلى اليمن، فقال لها أهله: ليس لك علينا نفقة. فانطلق خالد بن الوليد في نفر، فأتوا رسول الله ﷺ في بيت ميمونة، فقالوا: إن أبا حفص طلّق امرأته ثلاثاً، فهل لها من نفقة؟ فقال رسول الله ﷺ: (( ليست لها نفقة، وعليها العدة )). وأرسل إليها: (( أن لا تسبقيني بنفسك … )) الحديث. وفي لفظ: (( لا تفوتينا بنفسك )).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٣٨:١٤٨٠). وقوله: “لا تسبقيني” فيه التعريض بالخِطبة.

6275 — Abu Salamah reported that Fatimah bint Qays, the sister of al-Dahhak ibn Qays, informed him that Abu Hafs ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi divorced her three times, then left for Yemen. His family said to her: You have no maintenance due from us. So Khalid ibn al-Walid went with a group to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the house of Maymunah and said: Abu Hafs has divorced his wife three times, so does she have any maintenance? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “She has no maintenance, but she must observe the waiting period.” And he sent word to her: “Do not get ahead of us regarding yourself…” in the rest of the hadith. In another wording: “Do not let us miss the chance regarding yourself.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (38:1480). His saying “Do not get ahead of us regarding yourself” contains an indirect indication of proposing.

٦٢٧٦ — عن جابر بن عبد الله قال:

كان رسول الله ﷺ يعلمنا الاستخارة في الأمور كلها كما يعلمنا السورة من القرآن، يقول:

«إِذَا هَمَّ أَحَدُكُمْ بِالْأَمْرِ، فَلْيَرْكَعْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنْ غَيْرِ الْفَرِيضَةِ، ثُمَّ لِيَقُلْ:

اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْتَخِيرُكَ بِعِلْمِكَ، وَأَسْتَقْدِرُكَ بِقُدْرَتِكَ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ الْعَظِيمِ، فَإِنَّكَ تَقْدِرُ وَلَا أَقْدِرُ، وَتَعْلَمُ وَلَا أَعْلَمُ، وَأَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ.

6276 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh reported:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach us istikhārah concerning all matters just as he would teach us a surah from the Qurʾān. He would say:

“When one of you intends to undertake a matter, let him pray two rakʿahs other than the obligatory prayer, then say:

‘O Allah, I seek the better choice from You by Your knowledge, and I seek ability from You by Your power, and I ask You from Your immense bounty. You are able and I am not; You know and I do not know; and You are the Knower of the unseen.

O Allah, if You know that this matter is good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affair—or he said: in the immediate and later parts of my affair—then decree it for me, make it easy for me, and then bless it for me.

And if You know that this matter is bad for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affair—or he said: in the immediate and later parts of my affair—then turn it away from me and turn me away from it, decree good for me wherever it may be, and then make me content with it.’”

He said:

“And he should mention his particular need.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1162).

٦٢٧٧ — عن أيوب بن خالد بن أبي أيوب الأنصاري، حدثه عن أبيه، عن جده أبي أيوب أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: (( اكتم الخطبة، ثم توضأ فأحسن وضوءك، ثم صلِّ ما كتب الله لك، ثم احمد ربك، ومجِّده، ثم قل: اللهم إنك تقدر ولا أقدر، وتعلم ولا أعلم، وأنت علام الغيوب، فإن رأيت في فلانة - تسميها باسمها - خيراً لي في ديني ودنياي وآخرتي فاقدُرْها لي، وإن كان غيرُها خيراً لي منها في ديني ودنياي وآخرتي فاقض لي ذلك )).

حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٣٥٩٧)، وابن خزيمة (١٢٢٠)، وابن حبان (٤٠٤٠)، والحاكم (١/٣١٤).

6277 — Ayyub ibn Khalid ibn Abi Ayyub al-Ansari narrated from his father, from his grandfather Abu Ayyub, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Keep the proposal concealed, then perform ablution and do it well, then pray whatever Allah has prescribed for you, then praise your Lord and glorify Him, then say: O Allah, You are able and I am not able, and You know and I do not know, and You are the Knower of the unseen. If You know that there is good for me in so-and-so — naming her by name — in my religion, my worldly life, and my Hereafter, then decree her for me. And if someone other than her is better for me than her in my religion, my worldly life, and my Hereafter, then decree that for me.”

Hasan: Narrated by Ahmad (23597), Ibn Khuzaymah (1220), Ibn Hibban (4040), and al-Hakim (1/314).

٦٢٧٨ — عن سهل بن سعد:

أن امرأة جاءت إلى رسول الله ﷺ فقالت:

يا رسول الله، جئت لأهب لك نفسي.

فنظر إليها رسول الله ﷺ، فصعّد النظر إليها وصوّبه، ثم طأطأ رأسه.

فلما رأت المرأة أنه لم يقض فيها شيئًا جلست… الحديث.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥١٢٦)، ومسلم (١٤٢٥/٧٦).

٦٢٧٩ — عن أبي هريرة قال: كنت عند النبي ﷺ فأتاه رجل فأخبره أنه تزوّج امرأة من الأنصار. فقال له رسول الله ﷺ: (( أنظرت إليها؟ )) قال: لا، قال: (( فاذهب فانظر إليها، فإن في أعين الأنصار شيئاً )).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٧٤:١٤٢٤). قوله: (( في أعين الأنصار شيئاً )) قيل المراد بذلك صغر، وقيل زرقة.

english_source:
6279 — Abu Hurayrah said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ when a man came to him and informed him that he had married a woman from the Ansar. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: “Did you look at her?” He said: No. He said: “Then go and look at her, for there is something in the eyes of the Ansar.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (74:1424). His statement “there is something in the eyes of the Ansar” was said by some to mean smallness, and by others to mean a bluish tint.

٦٢٨٠ — عن أبي حميد أو أبي حميدة - وقد رأى رسول الله ﷺ - قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: (( إذا خطب أحدكم امرأة فلا جناح عليه أن ينظر إليها، إذا كان إنما ينظر لخطبة، وإن كانت لا تعلم )).

صحيح: رواه أحمد (٢٣٦٠٢).

6280 — Abu Humayd, or Abu Humaydah — and he had seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When one of you proposes to a woman, there is no blame on him if he looks at her, so long as he is only looking for the sake of marriage, even if she does not know.”

Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (23602).

٦٢٨١ — عن المغيرة بن شعبة، قال: أتيت النبي ﷺ، فذكرت له امرأة أخطبها، فقال: (( اذهب فانظر إليها، فإنه أجدر أن يُؤدم بينكما )). قال: فأتيت امرأة من الأنصار، فخطبتها إلى أبويها، وأخبرتهما بقول رسول الله ﷺ، فكأنهما كرها ذلك. قال: فسمعت ذلك المرأة وهي في خدرها، فقالت: إنْ كان رسول الله ﷺ أمرك أن تنظر، فانظر، وإلا فإني أنشدك. كأنها عظَّمت ذلك عليه. قال: فنظرتُ إليها فتزوجتُها. فذكر من موافقتها.

صحيح: رواه الترمذي (١٠٨٧)، والنسائي (٣٢٣٥)، وابن ماجه (١٨٦٦)، وأحمد (١٨١٣٧)، واللفظ له.

english_source:
6281 — Al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned to him a woman whom I intended to propose to. He said: “Go and look at her, for that is more likely to bring harmony between you.” He said: So I went to a woman from the Ansar and proposed to her through her parents, and I informed them of the statement of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It was as if they disliked that. Then the woman heard that while she was in her private chamber, and she said: If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded you to look, then look; otherwise, I place you under a solemn appeal. It was as though she regarded the matter as weighty for him. He said: So I looked at her and married her, and he mentioned her good compatibility.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (1087), al-Nasa’i (3235), Ibn Majah (1866), and Ahmad (18137). The wording is that of Ahmad.

٦٢٨٢ — عن جابر بن عبد الله الأنصاري قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: (( إذا خطب أحدكم المرأة، فقدر أن يرى منها بعض ما يدعوه إليها فليفعل )).

حسن: رواه الإمام أحمد (١٤٨٦٩).

Hasan: Narrated by Ahmad (14869).

٦٢٨٣ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال النبي ﷺ: (( إن الله كتب على ابن آدم حظه من الزنا، أدرك ذلك لا محالة، فزنا العين النظر، وزنا اللسان المنطق، والنفس تمني وتشتهي، والفرج يصدق ذلك كله ويكذبه )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٢٤٣) ومسلم (٢٦٥٧).

6283 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah has decreed for the son of Adam his share of adultery, and he will inevitably reach it. The adultery of the eye is looking, the adultery of the tongue is speaking, and the soul wishes and desires, while the private part confirms all of that or denies it.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (6243) and Muslim (2657).

6283 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah has decreed for the son of Adam his share of adultery, and he will inevitably reach it. The adultery of the eye is looking, the adultery of the tongue is speaking, and the soul wishes and desires, while the private part confirms all of that or denies it.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (6243) and Muslim (2657).

arabic_source:
٦٢٨٤ — عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ قال: (( كُتب على ابن آدم نصيبُه من الزنا، مدرك ذلك لا محالة، فالعينان زناهما النظر، والأذنان زناهما الاستماع، واللسان زناه الكلام، واليد زناها البطش، والرجل زناها الخطا، والقلب يهوى ويتمنى، ويصدق ذلك الفرج ويكذبه )).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢١:٢٦٥٧).

ورواه أبو داود (٢١٥٢) من وجه آخر به وزاد فيه: (( والفم يزني فزناه القبل )).

٦٢٨٨ — عن أبي برزة الأسلمي: أن جُليبيباً كان امرأً يدخل على النساء ويلاعبهن، فقلت لامرأتي: لا تدخلنَّ عليكم جُليبيبٌ، فإنه إن دخل عليكم لأفعلنَّ ولأفعلنَّ. قال: وكانت الأنصار إذا كان لأحدهم أيم، لم يزوّجها حتى يعلم هل للنبي ﷺ فيها حاجة أم لا. فقال رسول الله ﷺ لرجل من الأنصار: (( زوّجني ابنتك )). فقال: نعم وكرامةً يا رسول الله، ونِعْمَ عيني. قال: (( إني لست أريدها لنفسي )). قال: فلمن يا رسول الله؟ قال: (( لجُليبيب )).

قال: فقال: يا رسول الله، أشاور أمّها. فأتى أمّها، فقال: رسول الله ﷺ يخطب ابنتك. فقالت: نعم ونعمة عيني. فقال: إنه ليس يخطبها لنفسه، إنما خطبها لجليبيب. فقالت: أجُليبيبٌ إنيهِ؟ أجُليبيبٌ إنيهِ؟ أجُليبيبٌ إنيهِ؟ لا لعمرُ الله، لا نزوّجه. فلما أراد أن يقوم ليأتي رسول الله ﷺ فيخبره بما قالت أمُّها، قالت الجارية: من خطبني إليكم؟ فأخبرتها أمُّها. فقالت: أتردّون على رسول الله ﷺ أمره؟ ادفعوني، فإنه لم يضيّعني. فانطلق أبوها إلى رسول الله ﷺ فأخبره، فقال: (( شأنك بها )). فزوّجها جليبيباً.

صحيح: رواه الإمام أحمد (١٩٧٨٤).

english_source:
6288 — Abu Barzah al-Aslami reported that Julaybib was a man who used to enter among the women and joke with them, so I said to my wife: Do not let Julaybib enter upon you, for if he enters, I will certainly do such-and-such. He said: The Ansar, if one of them had an unmarried woman, would not marry her until they knew whether the Prophet ﷺ had any interest in her or not. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a man from the Ansar: “Marry your daughter to me.” He said: Yes, with honor, O Messenger of Allah, and gladly. He said: “I do not want her for myself.” He said: Then for whom, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “For Julaybib.”

He said: So he said: O Messenger of Allah, let me consult her mother. He went to her mother and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ is proposing for your daughter. She said: Yes, gladly and with full welcome. He said: He is not proposing for himself; he is proposing for Julaybib. She said: Julaybib? Him? Julaybib? Him? Julaybib? Him? No, by Allah, we will not marry her to him. When the father was about to leave to go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and tell him what her mother had said, the girl said: Who has proposed for me through you? Her mother told her. She said: Are you rejecting the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Give me in marriage, for he will not neglect me. So her father went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him, and he said: “The matter is yours with her.” So he married her to Julaybib.

Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (19784).

6288 — Abu Barzah al-Aslami reported that Julaybib was a man who used to enter among the women and joke with them, so I said to my wife: Do not let Julaybib enter upon you, for if he enters, I will certainly do such-and-such. He said: The Ansar, if one of them had an unmarried woman, would not marry her until they knew whether the Prophet ﷺ had any interest in her or not. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a man from the Ansar: “Marry your daughter to me.” He said: Yes, with honor, O Messenger of Allah, and gladly. He said: “I do not want her for myself.” He said: Then for whom, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “For Julaybib.”

He said: So he said: O Messenger of Allah, let me consult her mother. He went to her mother and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ is proposing for your daughter. She said: Yes, gladly and with full welcome. He said: He is not proposing for himself; he is proposing for Julaybib. She said: Julaybib? Him? Julaybib? Him? Julaybib? Him? No, by Allah, we will not marry her to him. When the father was about to leave to go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and tell him what her mother had said, the girl said: Who has proposed for me through you? Her mother told her. She said: Are you rejecting the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Give me in marriage, for he will not neglect me. So her father went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him, and he said: “The matter is yours with her.” So he married her to Julaybib.

Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (19784).

٦٢٨٩ — عن عائشة قالت:

جلس إحدى عشرة امرأة، فتعاهدن وتعاقدن أن لا يكتمن من أخبار أزواجهن شيئًا.

قالت الأولى: زوجي لحم جمل غث، على رأس جبل، لا سهل فيرتقى، ولا سمين فينتقل.

قالت الثانية: زوجي لا أبث خبره، إني أخاف أن لا أذره؛ إن أذكره أذكر عجره وبجره.

قالت الثالثة: زوجي العشنق، إن أنطق أطلق، وإن أسكت أعلق.

قالت الرابعة: زوجي كليل تهامة، لا حر ولا قر، ولا مخافة ولا سآمة.

قالت الخامسة: زوجي إن دخل فهد، وإن خرج أسد، ولا يسأل عما عهد.

قالت السادسة: زوجي إن أكل لف، وإن شرب اشتف، وإن اضطجع التف، ولا يولج الكف ليعلم البث.

قالت السابعة: زوجي غياياء - أو عياياء - طباقاء، كل داء له داء، شجك أو فلك أو جمع كلًّا لك.

قالت الثامنة: زوجي المس مس أرنب، والريح ريح زرنب.

قالت التاسعة: زوجي رفيع العماد، طويل النجاد، عظيم الرماد، قريب البيت من الناد.

قالت العاشرة: زوجي مالك، وما مالك؟ مالك خير من ذلك؛ له إبل كثيرات المبارك، قليلات المسارح، وإذا سمعن صوت المزهر أيقن أنهن هوالك.

قالت الحادية عشرة: زوجي أبو زرع، فما أبو زرع؟ أناس من حلي أذني، وملأ من شحم عضدي، وبجحني فبجحت إلي نفسي. وجدني في أهل غنيمة بشق، فجعلني في أهل صهيل وأطيط، ودائس ومنق. فعنده أقول فلا أقبح، وأرقد فأتصبح، وأشرب فأتقنح.

أم أبي زرع، فما أم أبي زرع؟ عكومها رداح، وبيتها فساح.

ابن أبي زرع، فما ابن أبي زرع؟ مضجعه كمسل شطبة، ويشبعه ذراع الجفرة.

بنت أبي زرع، فما بنت أبي زرع؟ طوع أبيها، وطوع أمها، وملء كسائها، وغيظ جارتها.

جارية أبي زرع، فما جارية أبي زرع؟ لا تبث حديثنا تبثيثًا، ولا تنقث ميرتنا تنقيثًا، ولا تملأ بيتنا تعشيشًا.

قالت: خرج أبو زرع والأوطاب تمخض، فلقي امرأة معها ولدان لها كالفهدين، يلعبان من تحت خصرها برمانتين، فطلقني ونكحها.

فنكحت بعده رجلًا سريًّا، ركب شريًّا، وأخذ خطيًّا، وأراح علي نعمًا ثريًّا، وأعطاني من كل رائحة زوجًا، وقال: كلي أم زرع، وميري أهلك.

قالت: فلو جمعت كل شيء أعطانيه، ما بلغ أصغر آنية أبي زرع.

قالت عائشة: قال رسول الله ﷺ:

«كُنْتُ لَكِ كَأَبِي زَرْعٍ لِأُمِّ زَرْعٍ».

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥١٨٩)، ومسلم (٢٤٤٨).

6289 — ʿĀʾishah reported:

Eleven women sat together and pledged to one another that they would conceal nothing concerning their husbands.

The first said: “My husband is like the meat of a lean camel on top of a mountain: the mountain is not easy to climb, nor is the meat fat enough to be worth carrying away.”

The second said: “I will not disclose the story of my husband, for I fear that if I begin, I will not finish. If I mention him, I will have to mention all his outward and inward faults.”

The third said: “My husband is tall and foolish. If I speak, I will be divorced; if I remain silent, I will be left suspended.”

The fourth said: “My husband is like the night of Tihāmah: neither hot nor cold, and there is neither fear nor weariness with him.”

The fifth said: “When my husband enters, he is like a leopard; when he goes out, he is like a lion, and he does not ask about what he has left behind.”

The sixth said: “When my husband eats, he devours everything; when he drinks, he drains it all; when he lies down, he wraps himself up, and he does not extend his hand to discover what troubles me.”

The seventh said: “My husband is foolish, helpless, and stupid. Every kind of defect is found in him. He may wound you, break you, or combine both against you.”

The eighth said: “The touch of my husband is like the touch of a rabbit, and his fragrance is like the fragrance of sweet basil.”

The ninth said: “My husband is lofty in his pillars, long in his sword-belt, great in his ashes, and his house is near the gathering place.”

The tenth said: “My husband is Mālik. And what is Mālik? Mālik is better than all that. He has many camels that remain near the house and few that are sent out to pasture. Whenever they hear the sound of the lute, they know that they are about to be slaughtered for guests.”

The eleventh said: “My husband is Abū Zarʿ. And what is Abū Zarʿ? He filled my ears with jewelry and filled my upper arms with flesh. He made me rejoice until I became pleased with myself. He found me among a poor family possessing only a few sheep in a narrow place, then brought me into a household of horses, camels, grain-threshing, and grain-cleaning. With him I speak and am not rebuked; I sleep until late in the morning; and I drink until I am completely satisfied.

The mother of Abū Zarʿ—and what is the mother of Abū Zarʿ? Her storage bags are large and full, and her house is spacious.

The son of Abū Zarʿ—and what is the son of Abū Zarʿ? His sleeping place is as slender as a drawn blade, and the foreleg of a young goat is enough to satisfy him.

The daughter of Abū Zarʿ—and what is the daughter of Abū Zarʿ? She is obedient to her father and obedient to her mother, fills out her garment, and causes her co-wife to feel jealous.

The servant-girl of Abū Zarʿ—and what is the servant-girl of Abū Zarʿ? She does not spread our secrets, does not waste our provisions, and does not fill our house with refuse.

Abū Zarʿ went out while the milk-skins were being churned and met a woman who had two children like little leopards, playing beneath her waist with two pomegranates. He divorced me and married her.

After him I married a noble man who rode a fine horse, carried an Indian spear, brought me abundant livestock, and gave me a pair of every kind. He said: ‘Eat, O Umm Zarʿ, and give provisions to your family.’

But even if I gathered together everything he gave me, it would not equal the smallest vessel of Abū Zarʿ.”

ʿĀʾishah said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:

“I am to you as Abū Zarʿ was to Umm Zarʿ.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5189) and Muslim (2448).

فنكحت بعده رجلًا سريًّا، ركب شريًّا، وأخذ خطيًّا، وأراح علي نعمًا ثريًّا، وأعطاني من كل رائحة زوجًا، وقال: كلي أم زرع، وميري أهلك.

قالت: فلو جمعت كل شيء أعطانيه، ما بلغ أصغر آنية أبي زرع.

قالت عائشة: قال رسول الله ﷺ:

«كُنْتُ لَكِ كَأَبِي زَرْعٍ لِأُمِّ زَرْعٍ».

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥١٨٩)، ومسلم (٢٤٤٨). 

6289 — ʿĀʾishah reported:

Eleven women sat together and pledged to one another that they would conceal nothing concerning their husbands.

The first said: “My husband is like the meat of a lean camel on top of a mountain: the mountain is not easy to climb, nor is the meat fat enough to be worth carrying away.”

The second said: “I will not disclose the story of my husband, for I fear that if I begin, I will not finish. If I mention him, I will have to mention all his outward and inward faults.”

The third said: “My husband is tall and foolish. If I speak, I will be divorced; if I remain silent, I will be left suspended.”

The fourth said: “My husband is like the night of Tihāmah: neither hot nor cold, and there is neither fear nor weariness with him.”

The fifth said: “When my husband enters, he is like a leopard; when he goes out, he is like a lion, and he does not ask about what he has left behind.”

The sixth said: “When my husband eats, he devours everything; when he drinks, he drains it all; when he lies down, he wraps himself up, and he does not extend his hand to discover what troubles me.”

The seventh said: “My husband is foolish, helpless, and stupid. Every kind of defect is found in him. He may wound you, break you, or combine both against you.”

The eighth said: “The touch of my husband is like the touch of a rabbit, and his fragrance is like the fragrance of sweet basil.”

The ninth said: “My husband is lofty in his pillars, long in his sword-belt, great in his ashes, and his house is near the gathering place.”

The tenth said: “My husband is Mālik. And what is Mālik? Mālik is better than all that. He has many camels that remain near the house and few that are sent out to pasture. Whenever they hear the sound of the lute, they know that they are about to be slaughtered for guests.”

The eleventh said: “My husband is Abū Zarʿ. And what is Abū Zarʿ? He filled my ears with jewelry and filled my upper arms with flesh. He made me rejoice until I became pleased with myself. He found me among a poor family possessing only a few sheep in a narrow place, then brought me into a household of horses, camels, grain-threshing, and grain-cleaning. With him I speak and am not rebuked; I sleep until late in the morning; and I drink until I am completely satisfied.

The mother of Abū Zarʿ—and what is the mother of Abū Zarʿ? Her storage bags are large and full, and her house is spacious.

The son of Abū Zarʿ—and what is the son of Abū Zarʿ? His sleeping place is as slender as a drawn blade, and the foreleg of a young goat is enough to satisfy him.

The daughter of Abū Zarʿ—and what is the daughter of Abū Zarʿ? She is obedient to her father and obedient to her mother, fills out her garment, and causes her co-wife to feel jealous.

The servant-girl of Abū Zarʿ—and what is the servant-girl of Abū Zarʿ? She does not spread our secrets, does not waste our provisions, and does not fill our house with refuse.

Abū Zarʿ went out while the milk-skins were being churned and met a woman who had two children like little leopards, playing beneath her waist with two pomegranates. He divorced me and married her.

After him I married a noble man who rode a fine horse, carried an Indian spear, brought me abundant livestock, and gave me a pair of every kind. He said: ‘Eat, O Umm Zarʿ, and give provisions to your family.’

But even if I gathered together everything he gave me, it would not equal the smallest vessel of Abū Zarʿ.”

ʿĀʾishah said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:

“I am to you as Abū Zarʿ was to Umm Zarʿ.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5189) and Muslim (2448).

٦٢٨٩ — عن عائشة قالت:

جلس إحدى عشرة امرأة، فتعاهدن وتعاقدن أن لا يكتمن من أخبار أزواجهن شيئًا.

قالت الأولى: زوجي لحم جمل غث، على رأس جبل، لا سهل فيرتقى، ولا سمين فينتقل.

قالت الثانية: زوجي لا أبث خبره، إني أخاف أن لا أذره؛ إن أذكره أذكر عجره وبجره.

قالت الثالثة: زوجي العشنق، إن أنطق أطلق، وإن أسكت أعلق.

قالت الرابعة: زوجي كليل تهامة، لا حر ولا قر، ولا مخافة ولا سآمة.

قالت الخامسة: زوجي إن دخل فهد، وإن خرج أسد، ولا يسأل عما عهد.

قالت السادسة: زوجي إن أكل لف، وإن شرب اشتف، وإن اضطجع التف، ولا يولج الكف ليعلم البث.

قالت السابعة: زوجي غياياء - أو عياياء - طباقاء، كل داء له داء، شجك أو فلك أو جمع كلًّا لك.

قالت الثامنة: زوجي المس مس أرنب، والريح ريح زرنب.

قالت التاسعة: زوجي رفيع العماد، طويل النجاد، عظيم الرماد، قريب البيت من الناد.

قالت العاشرة: زوجي مالك، وما مالك؟ مالك خير من ذلك؛ له إبل كثيرات المبارك، قليلات المسارح، وإذا سمعن صوت المزهر أيقن أنهن هوالك.

قالت الحادية عشرة: زوجي أبو زرع، فما أبو زرع؟ أناس من حلي أذني، وملأ من شحم عضدي، وبجحني فبجحت إلي نفسي. وجدني في أهل غنيمة بشق، فجعلني في أهل صهيل وأطيط، ودائس ومنق. فعنده أقول فلا أقبح، وأرقد فأتصبح، وأشرب فأتقنح.

أم أبي زرع، فما أم أبي زرع؟ عكومها رداح، وبيتها فساح.

ابن أبي زرع، فما ابن أبي زرع؟ مضجعه كمسل شطبة، ويشبعه ذراع الجفرة.

بنت أبي زرع، فما بنت أبي زرع؟ طوع أبيها، وطوع أمها، وملء كسائها، وغيظ جارتها.

٦٢٩٠ — عن النعمان بن بشير قال: استأذن أبو بكر على النبي ﷺ، فسمع صوت عائشة عاليا، فلما دخل تناولها ليلطمها، وقال: ألا أراك ترفعين صوتك على رسول الله ﷺ، فجعل النبي ﷺ يحجزه، وخرج أبو بكر مغضبا، فقال النبي ﷺ حين خرج أبو بكر: (( كيف رأيتني أنقذتك من الرجل؟ )) قال: فمكث أبو بكر أياما، ثم استأذن على رسول الله ﷺ فوجدهما قد اصطلحا، فقال لهما: أدخلاني في سلمكما كما أدخلتماني في حربكما. فقال النبي ﷺ: (( قد فعلنا، قد فعلنا )).

صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٤٩٩٩) وأحمد (١٨٣٩٤)، واللفظ لأبي داود. ولم يذكر أحمد قوله: (( قد فعلنا، قد فعلنا )).

6290 — Al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir said: Abu Bakr asked permission to enter upon the Prophet ﷺ and heard the voice of ‘A’ishah raised. When he entered, he moved toward her to slap her and said: Do I see you raising your voice over the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? The Prophet ﷺ began restraining him, and Abu Bakr left angry. When Abu Bakr left, the Prophet ﷺ said: “How did you find that I rescued you from the man?” He said: Abu Bakr stayed away for some days, then asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found that the two had reconciled. So he said to them: Let me enter into your peace just as you made me enter into your conflict. The Prophet ﷺ said: “We have done so, we have done so.”

Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud (4999) and Ahmad (18394). The wording is that of Abu Dawud. Ahmad did not mention the words, “We have done so, we have done so.”

٦٢٩١ — عن ابن عباس قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي ﷺ فقال: إن امرأتي لا تمنع يد لامس. فقال: (( غَرِّبْها إن شئت )). قال: إني أخاف أن تتبعها نفسي، قال: (( استمتع بها )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٠٤٩) والنسائي (٣٤٦٤) والبيهقي (٧/١٥٤).

6291 — Ibn ‘Abbas said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: My wife does not refuse the hand of one who touches. He said: “Divorce her if you wish.” The man said: I fear that my soul will still follow after her. He said: “Then continue to live with her.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2049), al-Nasa’i (3464), and al-Bayhaqi (7/154).

٦٢٩٢ — عن جابر بن عبد الله أن رجلا أتى رسول الله ﷺ فقال: يا رسول الله ﷺ إن لي امرأة وهي لا تدفع يد لامس. قال: (( طلِّقها )). قال: إني أحبها وهي جميلة. قال: (( فاستمتع بها )).

حسن: رواه البيهقي في السنن الكبرى (٧/١٥٥-١٥٤).

وقوله: (( لا تمنع يدَ لامس )) معناه أن الرجل وقع في قلبه ريبة منها، وفي الوقت نفسه لا يستطيع مفارقتها، فأمر النبي ﷺ بالبقاء معها، والصبر عليها، لعلها يتحسن حالها.

وقول النبي ﷺ: (( استمتع بها )) إشارة إلى كثرة الجماع منها لكسر شهوتها. والله تعالى أعلم.

٦٢٩٢ — عن جابر بن عبد الله أن رجلا أتى رسول الله ﷺ فقال: يا رسول الله ﷺ إن لي امرأة وهي لا تدفع يد لامس. قال: (( طلِّقها )). قال: إني أحبها وهي جميلة. قال: (( فاستمتع بها )).

حسن: رواه البيهقي في السنن الكبرى (٧/١٥٥-١٥٤).

وقوله: (( لا تمنع يدَ لامس )) معناه أن الرجل وقع في قلبه ريبة منها، وفي الوقت نفسه لا يستطيع مفارقتها، فأمر النبي ﷺ بالبقاء معها، والصبر عليها، لعلها يتحسن حالها.

وقول النبي ﷺ: (( استمتع بها )) إشارة إلى كثرة الجماع منها لكسر شهوتها. والله تعالى أعلم.

6292 — Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah reported that a man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I have a wife and she does not push away the hand of one who touches. He said: “Divorce her.” The man said: I love her and she is beautiful. He said: “Then continue to live with her.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/154–155).

His statement, “she does not prevent the hand of one who touches,” means that suspicion had entered the man’s heart regarding her, while at the same time he could not bear to part from her. So the Prophet ﷺ instructed him to remain with her and be patient, in hopes that her condition might improve.

The Prophet’s ﷺ statement, “continue to live with her,” is an indication of increasing intimacy with her in order to restrain her desire. And Allah Most High knows best.

٦٢٩٤ — عن عائشة قالت: كنت ألعب بالبنات عند النبي ﷺ، وكان لي صواحب يلعبْنَ معي. فكان رسول الله ﷺ إذا دخل يتقَمّعْن منه، فيُسَرِّبُهُنَّ إليَّ فيلعبْن معي.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦١٣٠) ومسلم (٢٤٤٠).

وقولها: (( كنت ألعب بالبنات )) فيه جواز اللعب بالدُّمية.

وقولها: (( يتقَمّعْن )) أي يتغيَّبْن حياءً منه وهيبةً.

وقولها: (( يسربهنّ )) أي يرسلهن ويدفعهن إليّ.

6294 — ‘A’ishah said: I used to play with dolls in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and I had girl-friends who played with me. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered, they would hide from him, and he would send them to me so they could play with me.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (6130) and Muslim (2440).

Her statement, “I used to play with dolls,” shows the permissibility of playing with dolls.

Her statement, “they would hide,” means they would withdraw out of modesty and awe toward him.

Her statement, “he would send them,” means he would send them over and let them come to me.

٦٢٩٥ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال:

«مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ، فَإِذَا شَهِدَ أَمْرًا فَلْيَتَكَلَّمْ بِخَيْرٍ أَوْ لِيَسْكُتْ، وَاسْتَوْصُوا بِالنِّسَاءِ، فَإِنَّ الْمَرْأَةَ خُلِقَتْ مِنْ ضِلَعٍ، وَإِنَّ أَعْوَجَ شَيْءٍ فِي الضِّلَعِ أَعْلَاهُ، إِنْ ذَهَبْتَ تُقِيمُهُ كَسَرْتَهُ، وَإِنْ تَرَكْتَهُ لَمْ يَزَلْ أَعْوَجَ، اسْتَوْصُوا بِالنِّسَاءِ خَيْرًا».

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥١٨٥-٥١٨٦)، ومسلم (١٤٦٨/٦٠)، واللفظ لمسلم.

ورواه مسلم من وجه آخر بلفظ:

«إِنَّ الْمَرْأَةَ كَالضِّلَعِ، إِذَا ذَهَبْتَ تُقِيمُهَا كَسَرْتَهَا، وَإِنْ تَرَكْتَهَا اسْتَمْتَعْتَ بِهَا وَفِيهَا عِوَجٌ».

6295 — Abū Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:

“Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, when he is present at a matter, let him speak good or remain silent. Treat women well, for woman was created from a rib, and the most crooked part of the rib is its upper part. If you try to straighten it, you will break it; and if you leave it, it will remain crooked. So treat women well.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5185–5186) and Muslim (1468/60). This is Muslim’s wording.

Muslim also narrated through another route:

“Woman is like a rib. If you try to straighten her, you will break her; and if you leave her, you may enjoy life with her while crookedness remains in her.”

«إِنَّ الْمَرْأَةَ كَالضِّلَعِ، إِذَا ذَهَبْتَ تُقِيمُهَا كَسَرْتَهَا، وَإِنْ تَرَكْتَهَا اسْتَمْتَعْتَ بِهَا وَفِيهَا عِوَجٌ». 

6295 — Abū Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:

“Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, when he is present at a matter, let him speak good or remain silent. Treat women well, for woman was created from a rib, and the most crooked part of the rib is its upper part. If you try to straighten it, you will break it; and if you leave it, it will remain crooked. So treat women well.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5185–5186) and Muslim (1468/60). This is Muslim’s wording.

Muslim also narrated through another route:

“Woman is like a rib. If you try to straighten her, you will break her; and if you leave her, you may enjoy life with her while crookedness remains in her.”

6297 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A believing man should not hate a believing woman. If he dislikes one trait in her, he will be pleased with another,” or he said, “with a different one.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1469).

His statement, “should not hate,” means should not loathe or detest. It is said in Arabic: he hated him, meaning he came to dislike him.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3330) and Muslim (63:1470), with this wording from Muslim.

His statement, “and meat would not rot,” means it would not become foul-smelling and change.

٦٣٠٠ — عن جابر بن عبد الله قال في حديث حجة الوداع:

حتى إذا زاغت الشمس أمر بالقصواء، فرحلت له، فأتى بطن الوادي، فخطب الناس وقال:

«إِنَّ دِمَاءَكُمْ وَأَمْوَالَكُمْ حَرَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ كَحُرْمَةِ يَوْمِكُمْ هَذَا، فِي شَهْرِكُمْ هَذَا، فِي بَلَدِكُمْ هَذَا.

أَلَا كُلُّ شَيْءٍ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ تَحْتَ قَدَمَيَّ مَوْضُوعٌ، وَدِمَاءُ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ مَوْضُوعَةٌ، وَإِنَّ أَوَّلَ دَمٍ أَضَعُ مِنْ دِمَائِنَا دَمُ ابْنِ رَبِيعَةَ بْنِ الْحَارِثِ - كَانَ يُسْتَرْضَعُ فِي بَنِي سَعْدٍ، فَقَتَلَتْهُ هُذَيْلٌ - وَرِبَا الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ مَوْضُوعٌ، وَأَوَّلُ رِبًا أَضَعُ رِبَانَا، رِبَا عَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ، فَإِنَّهُ مَوْضُوعٌ كُلُّهُ.

فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ فِي النِّسَاءِ، فَإِنَّكُمْ أَخَذْتُمُوهُنَّ بِأَمَانِ اللَّهِ، وَاسْتَحْلَلْتُمْ فُرُوجَهُنَّ بِكَلِمَةِ اللَّهِ، وَلَكُمْ عَلَيْهِنَّ أَنْ لَا يُوطِئْنَ فُرُشَكُمْ أَحَدًا تَكْرَهُونَهُ، فَإِنْ فَعَلْنَ ذَلِكَ فَاضْرِبُوهُنَّ ضَرْبًا غَيْرَ مُبَرِّحٍ، وَلَهُنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ رِزْقُهُنَّ وَكِسْوَتُهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ…»

صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٢١٨).

6300 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh reported in the hadith of the Farewell Pilgrimage:

When the sun had passed its zenith, the Prophet ﷺ ordered that al-Qaṣwāʾ be saddled for him. He came to the middle of the valley and addressed the people, saying:

“Your blood and your wealth are sacred to one another, just as this day of yours is sacred, in this month of yours, in this land of yours.

Everything from the affairs of the pre-Islamic period is placed beneath my feet and abolished. The blood claims of the pre-Islamic period are abolished, and the first blood claim of ours that I abolish is that of the son of Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith—he had been sent to be nursed among Banū Saʿd and was killed by Hudhayl.

The usury of the pre-Islamic period is abolished, and the first usury of ours that I abolish is that of al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. All of it is abolished.

Fear Allah regarding women, for you have taken them under the trust of Allah and made marital relations with them lawful by the word of Allah.

Your right over them is that they do not allow onto your bedding anyone whom you dislike. If they do so, then strike them in a manner that is not severe. Their right over you is that you provide them with food and clothing according to what is reasonable…”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1218).

«إِنَّ دِمَاءَكُمْ وَأَمْوَالَكُمْ حَرَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ كَحُرْمَةِ يَوْمِكُمْ هَذَا، فِي شَهْرِكُمْ هَذَا، فِي بَلَدِكُمْ هَذَا.

أَلَا كُلُّ شَيْءٍ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ تَحْتَ قَدَمَيَّ مَوْضُوعٌ، وَدِمَاءُ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ مَوْضُوعَةٌ، وَإِنَّ أَوَّلَ دَمٍ أَضَعُ مِنْ دِمَائِنَا دَمُ ابْنِ رَبِيعَةَ بْنِ الْحَارِثِ - كَانَ يُسْتَرْضَعُ فِي بَنِي سَعْدٍ، فَقَتَلَتْهُ هُذَيْلٌ - وَرِبَا الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ مَوْضُوعٌ، وَأَوَّلُ رِبًا أَضَعُ رِبَانَا، رِبَا عَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ، فَإِنَّهُ مَوْضُوعٌ كُلُّهُ.

٦٣٠١ — عن عائشة قالت: كنت أشرب وأنا حائض، ثم أناوله النبي ﷺ فيضع فاه موضع فيَّ، فيشرب وأتعرق العَرْق وأنا حائض، ثم أناوله النبي ﷺ فيضع فاه موضع فيَّ.

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٣٠٠).

والعَرْق - بسكون الراء - إذا أخذ عنه معظم اللحم وجمعه عُراق. وقيل: هو العظم الذي عليه بقية من لحم. وفيه مداراة النبي ﷺ من مؤاكلة أهله وشربه.

6301 — ‘A’ishah said: I would drink while menstruating, then hand it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he would place his mouth where mine had been and drink. And I would gnaw meat from a bone while menstruating, then hand it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he would place his mouth where mine had been.

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (300).

The word ‘irq with a silent ra’ means a bone from which most of the meat has been taken, and its plural is ‘iraq. It was also said that it means a bone that still has some meat on it. In this is the Prophet’s ﷺ gentle companionship in eating and drinking with his family.

٦٣٠٢ — عن عائشة قالت: سابقني النبي ﷺ فسبقته، فلبثنا حتى إذا أرهقني اللحم سابقني فسبقني. فقال النبي ﷺ: (( هذه بتلك)).

6302 — ‘A’ishah said: The Prophet ﷺ raced me, and I beat him. Then time passed until I had put on weight, and he raced me and beat me. So the Prophet ﷺ said: “This is for that.”

Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2578), Ibn Majah (1979), and authenticated by Ibn Hibban (4691).

٦٣٠٣ — عن عائشة قالت: خرجت مع النبي ﷺ في بعض أسفاره وأنا جارية لم أحمل اللحم ولم أبدُنْ، فقال للناس: (( تقدموا )) فتقدموا. ثم قال لي: (( تعالي حتى أسابقك )) فسابقته فسبقته، فسكت عني حتى إذا حملت اللحم، وبدنت، ونسيت، خرجت معه في بعض أسفاره، فقال للناس: (( تقدموا )) فتقدموا ثم قال: (( تعالي حتى أسابقك )) فسابقته فسبقني، فجعل يضحك وهو يقول: (( هذه بتلك )).

حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٦٢٧٧).

english_source:
6303 — ‘A’ishah said: I went out with the Prophet ﷺ on one of his journeys while I was still a young girl, not carrying flesh and not heavy in body. He said to the people: “Go ahead,” so they went ahead. Then he said to me: “Come, so I may race you.” So I raced him and beat him. He said nothing to me about it until later, when I had put on flesh, gained weight, and forgotten about it. Then I went out with him on another journey, and he said to the people: “Go ahead,” so they went ahead. Then he said: “Come, so I may race you.” So I raced him and he beat me, and he began laughing, saying: “This is for that.”

Hasan: Narrated by Ahmad (26277).

6304 — ‘A’ishah said: I brought the Messenger of Allah ﷺ some khazirah that I had cooked for him, and I said to Sawdah—while the Prophet ﷺ was between me and her—“Eat.” She refused. I said: “Either you eat, or I will smear your face.” She still refused, so I put my hand in the khazirah and smeared her face. The Prophet ﷺ laughed, then he put his hand for her and said to her: “Smear her face.” So the Prophet ﷺ laughed with her. Then ‘Umar passed by and said: “O servant of Allah, O servant of Allah!” and he thought that he would come in. So he said: “Get up and wash your faces.” ‘A’ishah said: I continued to stand in awe of ‘Umar because of the Messenger of Allah’s ﷺ awe of him.

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Ya‘la (4476) and Abu Bakr al-Shafi‘i in al-Ghaylaniyyat (117).

Khazirah is a food cooked from meat and flour, somewhat like a thick porridge.

٦٣٠٥ — عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: (( إن أعظم الذنوب عند الله رجل تزوج امرأة فلما قضى حاجته طَلَّقَها، فذهب بمهرها، ورجل استعمل رجلا فذهب بأجرته، وآخر يقتل دابة عبثا )).

حسن: رواه الحاكم (٢/١٨٢).

english_source:
6305 — Ibn ʿUmar reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“Among the gravest sins in the sight of Allah is that a man marries a woman, then, after satisfying his desire with her, divorces her and takes away her dowry; that a man employs another man and then deprives him of his wages; and that a person kills an animal for no purpose.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Ḥākim (2/182).

٦٣٠٦ — عن أبي ذر، عن النبي ﷺ قال: «وفي بُضع أحدكم صدقة». قالوا: يا رسول الله! أيأتي أحدنا شهوته، ويكون له فيه أجر؟ فقال: «أرأيتم لو وضعها في الحرام أكان عليه وزر؟ فكذلك إذا وضعها في الحلال، كان له أجر».

صحيح: رواه مسلم في الزكاة (١٠٠٦).

english_source:
6306 — Abū Dharr reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:

“And in the sexual intimacy of each one of you there is an act of charity.”

They said, “O Messenger of Allah! Does one of us fulfill his desire and receive a reward for it?”

He ﷺ said:

“Tell me, if he were to satisfy it in what is unlawful, would he bear a sin for that? Likewise, when he satisfies it in what is lawful, he receives a reward.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim in The Book of Zakāh (1006).

٦٣٠٧ — عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: (( يا عبد الله، ألم أخبر أنك تصوم النهار وتقوم الليل؟ )) قلت: بلى يا رسول الله، قال: (( فلا تفعل، صُمْ وأفطر، وقُمْ ونَمْ، فإنَّ لجسدك عليك حقاً، وإن لعينك عليك حقاً، وإنّ لزوجك عليك حقاً )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥١٩٩)، ومسلم (١١٥٩).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥١٩٩)، ومسلم (١١٥٩).
english_source:
6307 — ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘As said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O ‘Abd Allah, have I not been told that you fast by day and stand in prayer by night?” I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “Do not do that. Fast and break your fast. Stand in prayer and sleep. For your body has a right over you, your eyes have a right over you, and your wife has a right over you.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5199) and Muslim (1159).

٦٣٠٨ — عن أبي جُحيفة قال: آخى النبي ﷺ بين سلمان وأبي الدرداء، فزار سلمان أبا الدرداء فرأى أم الدرداء متبذّلة، فقال لها: ما شأنك؟ قالت: أخوك أبو الدرداء ليس له حاجة في الدنيا. فجاء أبو الدرداء فصنع له طعاماً، فقال: كل فإني صائم. قال: ما أنا بآكل حتى تأكل. فأكل، فلما كان الليل هب أبو الدرداء يقوم، قال: نمْ، فنام، ثم ذهب يقوم فقال: نَمْ. فلما كان آخر الليل قال سلمان: قمْ الآن. فصلّيا فقال له سلمان: إن لربك عليك حقا، ولنفسك عليك حقا، ولأهلك عليك حقا، فأعط كل ذي حق حقه. فأتى النبي ﷺ فذكر ذلك له، فقال النبي ﷺ: (( صدق سلمان )).

صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٩٦٨).

english_source:
6308 — Abu Juhayfah said: The Prophet ﷺ made Salman and Abu al-Darda’ brothers. Salman visited Abu al-Darda’ and saw Umm al-Darda’ in worn clothing, so he said to her: What is the matter with you? She said: Your brother Abu al-Darda’ has no interest in worldly things. Then Abu al-Darda’ came and prepared food for him. Abu al-Darda’ said: Eat, for I am fasting. Salman said: I will not eat until you eat. So Abu al-Darda’ ate. When night came, Abu al-Darda’ got up to pray, but Salman said: Sleep. So he slept. Then he got up again, and Salman said: Sleep. Then at the end of the night Salman said: Now get up. So they prayed. Then Salman said to him: Your Lord has a right over you, your self has a right over you, and your family has a right over you, so give each possessor of a right his right. Then Abu al-Darda’ came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Salman has spoken the truth.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (1968).

٦٣٠٨ — عن أبي جُحيفة قال: آخى النبي ﷺ بين سلمان وأبي الدرداء، فزار سلمان أبا الدرداء فرأى أم الدرداء متبذّلة، فقال لها: ما شأنك؟ قالت: أخوك أبو الدرداء ليس له حاجة في الدنيا. فجاء أبو الدرداء فصنع له طعاماً، فقال: كل فإني صائم. قال: ما أنا بآكل حتى تأكل. فأكل، فلما كان الليل هب أبو الدرداء يقوم، قال: نمْ، فنام، ثم ذهب يقوم فقال: نَمْ. فلما كان آخر الليل قال سلمان: قمْ الآن. فصلّيا فقال له سلمان: إن لربك عليك حقا، ولنفسك عليك حقا، ولأهلك عليك حقا، فأعط كل ذي حق حقه. فأتى النبي ﷺ فذكر ذلك له، فقال النبي ﷺ: (( صدق سلمان )).

٦٣١٠ — عن حكيم بن معاوية القُشيري، عن أبيه قال: قلت: يا رسول الله! ما حق زوجة أحدنا عليه؟ قال: (( أن تُطعمها إذا طعمتَ، وتكسوها إذا اكتسيت، ولا تضرب الوجه، ولا تُقبِّح، ولا تهجر إلا في البيت )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢١٤٢) وابن ماجه (١٨٥٠) وصححه ابن حبان (٤١٧٥) والحاكم (٢/١٨٧-١٨٨).

6310 — Hakim ibn Mu‘awiyah al-Qushayri reported from his father that he said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of one of our wives over him? He said: “That you feed her when you eat, clothe her when you clothe yourself, do not strike the face, do not revile her, and do not forsake her except within the house.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2142), Ibn Majah (1850), authenticated by Ibn Hibban (4175), and al-Hakim (2/187–188).

٦٣١١ — عن عائشة قالت: جاءت هند بنتُ عتبة إلى النبي ﷺ، فقالت: يا رسول الله، والله ما كان على ظهر الأرض أهل خباء أحبّ إلي من أن يذلهم الله من أهل خبائك، وما على ظهر الأرض أهل خباء أحب إلي من أن يعزهم الله من أهل خبائك، فقال النبي ﷺ: (( وأيضا والذي نفسي بيده )) ثم قالت: يا رسول الله، إن أبا سفيان رجلٌ ممسكٌ، فهل عليَّ حرجٌ أن أُنفِقَ على عياله من ماله بغير إذنه؟ فقال النبي ﷺ: (( لا حرجَ عليكِ أن تنفقي عليهم بالمعروف )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٨٢٥)، ومسلم (٨:١٧١٤) والسياق لمسلم، وسياق البخاري قريب منه.

english_source:
6311 — ‘A’ishah said: Hind bint ‘Utbah came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, there was no household on the face of the earth more beloved to me that Allah should disgrace than your household, and now there is no household on the face of the earth more beloved to me that Allah should honor than your household. The Prophet ﷺ said: “And also, by the One in whose hand is my soul.” Then she said: O Messenger of Allah, Abu Sufyan is a stingy man. Is there any sin upon me if I spend on his dependents from his wealth without his permission? The Prophet ﷺ said: “There is no sin upon you to spend on them in a fair manner.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3825) and Muslim (8:1714), with this wording from Muslim. Al-Bukhari’s wording is close to it.

Hasan: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (1162), Abu Dawud (4682), authenticated by Ibn Hibban (4176), and al-Hakim (1/3).

٦٣١٣ — عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله ﷺ:

«خَيْرُكُمْ خَيْرُكُمْ لِأَهْلِهِ، وَأَنَا خَيْرُكُمْ لِأَهْلِي، وَإِذَا مَاتَ صَاحِبُكُمْ فَدَعُوهُ».

صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٣٨٩٥)، وصححه ابن حبان (٤١٧٧)، وأبو نعيم في الحلية (٧/١٣٨).
arabic_display:
٦٣١٣ — عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله ﷺ:

«خَيْرُكُمْ خَيْرُكُمْ لِأَهْلِهِ، وَأَنَا خَيْرُكُمْ لِأَهْلِي، وَإِذَا مَاتَ صَاحِبُكُمْ فَدَعُوهُ».

صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٣٨٩٥)، وصححه ابن حبان (٤١٧٧)، وأبو نعيم في الحلية (٧/١٣٨).
english_source:
6313 — ʿĀʾishah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“The best of you are those who are best to their families, and I am the best of you to my family. When your companion dies, leave him alone.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3895), authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (4177), and narrated by Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilyah (7/138).

٦٣١٤ — عن أم سلمة، أن النبي ﷺ حلف لا يدخل على بعض أهله شهراً، فلما مضى تسعة وعشرون يوماً غدا عليهنّ أو راح، فقيل له: يا نبي الله، حلفت أن لا تدخل عليهن شهراً؟ قال: (( إن الشهر يكون تسعة وعشرين يوماً )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٢٠٢)، ومسلم (٢٥:١٠٨٥).

6314 — Umm Salamah reported that the Prophet ﷺ swore that he would not enter upon some of his wives for one month. Then when twenty-nine days had passed, he came to them in the morning or evening. It was said to him: O Prophet of Allah, you swore that you would not enter upon them for a month. He said: “The month may be twenty-nine days.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5202) and Muslim (25:1085).

٦٣١٥ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: (( إذا دعا الرجل امرأته إلى فراشه، فأبت أن تجيءَ لعنتها الملائكة حتى تصبح )). وفي رواية: (( إذا باتت المرأة مهاجرةً فراش زوجها، لعنتها الملائكة حتى ترجع )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥١٩٣)، ومسلم (١٢:١٤٣٦)، واللفظ للبخاري.
