6495 — ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb reported from his father, from his grandfather:

Marthad ibn Abī Marthad al-Ghanawī was a strong man who used to carry Muslim captives from Makkah to Madinah.

He said:

I arranged to carry a man out, and in Makkah there was a prostitute called ʿAnāq who had formerly been my companion.

She came out and saw my silhouette in the shadow of the wall and said:

“Who is this? Marthad? Welcome, Marthad! Come tonight and spend the night with us at the camp.”

I replied:

“O ʿAnāq, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has forbidden fornication.”

She cried out:

“O people of the tents! This is the duldul who carries your captives from Makkah to Madinah!”

I took the route of al-Khandamah, and eight men pursued me. They came until they stood directly above my head and urinated, and their urine splashed upon me, but Allah blinded them to my presence.

I then went to my companion and carried him away. When I reached al-Arāk, I removed his shackles.

Then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked:

“O Messenger of Allah, may I marry ʿAnāq?”

He remained silent until the verse was revealed:

“The fornicatress is not married except by a fornicator or a polytheist.”  [al-Nūr: 3]

He recited it to me and said:

“Do not marry her.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (2051), al-Nasāʾī (3228), al-Tirmidhī (3176), who graded it Hasan, and al-Ṭaḥāwī in Mushkil al-Āthār (4552). 

Al-Azraqī said:

Al-duldul means a hedgehog, which most often appears at night and conceals its head.

Al-Khandamah is a mountain behind Abū Qubays.

٦٤٩٦ — عن عبد الله بن عمرو أن رجلاً من المسلمين استأذن رسول الله ﷺ في امرأة يقال لها: “أم مهزول” وكانت تُسافح، وتشترط للرجل يتزوجها أن تكفيه النفقة، فاستأذن رسول الله ﷺ، أو ذكر له أمرها. قال: فقرأ عليه نبي الله ﷺ: (وَٱلزَّانِيَةُ لَا يَنكِحُهَا إِلَّا زَانٍ أَوْ مُشْرِكٌ) [النور: ٣].

٦٤٩٩ — عن أنس أن عبد الرحمن بن عوف تزوج امرأة على وزن نواة، فرأى النبي ﷺ بشاشة العُرس، فسأله، فقال: إني تزوجت امرأة على وزن نواة.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥١٤٨)، ومسلم (٨٢:١٤٢٧). وزاد البخاري: على وزن نواة من ذهب.

ونواة: قيمتها خمسة دراهم. وفي رواية قال أنس: فلقد رأيته قسّم لكل امرأة من نسائه بعد موته مائة ألف.

6499 — Anas narrated that ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf married a woman for the weight of a date-stone. The Prophet ﷺ saw the signs of marriage happiness on him and asked him, and he said: I have married a woman for the weight of a date-stone.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5148) and Muslim (1427 no. 82). Al-Bukhari added: the weight of a date-stone of gold.

A date-stone was valued at five dirhams. In another narration, Anas said: I indeed saw that after his death, one hundred thousand was apportioned to each of his wives.

٦٥٠٠ — عن سهل بن سعد قال:

جاءت امرأة إلى رسول الله ﷺ فقالت: يا رسول الله، جئت أهب لك نفسي.

فنظر إليها رسول الله ﷺ فصعّد النظر فيها وصوّبه، ثم طأطأ رأسه.

فلما رأت المرأة أنه لم يقض فيها شيئًا جلست، فقام رجل من أصحابه فقال: يا رسول الله، إن لم يكن لك بها حاجة فزوّجنيها.

فقال:

«هَلْ عِنْدَكَ شَيْءٌ؟»

قال: لا والله يا رسول الله.

قال:

«اذْهَبْ إِلَى أَهْلِكَ فَانْظُرْ هَلْ تَجِدُ شَيْئًا».

فذهب ثم رجع فقال: لا والله، ما وجدت شيئًا.

فقال رسول الله ﷺ:

«انْظُرْ وَلَوْ خَاتَمًا مِنْ حَدِيدٍ».

فذهب ثم رجع فقال: لا والله يا رسول الله، ولا خاتمًا من حديد، ولكن هذا إزاري - قال سهل: ما له رداء - فلها نصفه.

فقال رسول الله ﷺ:

«مَا تَصْنَعُ بِإِزَارِكَ؟ إِنْ لَبِسْتَهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْهَا مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ، وَإِنْ لَبِسَتْهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْكَ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ».

فجلس الرجل، حتى إذا طال مجلسه قام، فرآه رسول الله ﷺ مولّيًا، فأمر به فدعي له.

فلما جاء قال:

«مَا مَعَكَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ؟»

قال: معي سورة كذا وسورة كذا، عدّدها.

فقال:

«تَقْرَؤُهُنَّ عَنْ ظَهْرِ قَلْبٍ؟»

قال: نعم.

قال:

«اذْهَبْ، فَقَدْ مَلَّكْتُكَهَا بِمَا مَعَكَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ».

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٠٨٧)، ومسلم (١٤٢٥).

وفي لفظ مسلم:

«انْطَلِقْ، فَقَدْ زَوَّجْتُكَهَا، فَعَلِّمْهَا مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ».

6500 — Sahl ibn Saʿd reported:

A woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:

“O Messenger of Allah, I have come to offer myself to you.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at her, raising and lowering his gaze, then lowered his head.

When the woman saw that he had made no decision concerning her, she sat down.

A man from among his Companions stood up and said:

“O Messenger of Allah, if you have no need of her, then marry her to me.”

He asked:

“Do you have anything?”

He replied:

“No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah.”

He said:

“Go to your family and see whether you can find anything.”

He went and then returned and said:

“No, by Allah, I found nothing.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“Look, even if it is only an iron ring.”

He went and returned and said:

“No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, not even an iron ring. But I have this lower garment”—Sahl said that he had no upper garment—“and she may have half of it.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“What would she do with your lower garment? If you wear it, she will have none of it; and if she wears it, you will have none of it.”

The man sat down. After he had remained seated for a long time, he got up to leave.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him turning away and ordered that he be called back.

When he returned, he asked:

“What do you know of the Qurʾān?”

He replied:

“I know such-and-such surah and such-and-such surah,” and he listed them.

He asked:

“Do you recite them from memory?”

He replied:

“Yes.”

He said:

“Go. I have married her to you for what you know of the Qurʾān.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5087) and Muslim (1425).

In Muslim’s wording:

“Go, for I have married her to you, so teach her from the Qurʾān.”

فنظر إليها رسول الله ﷺ فصعّد النظر فيها وصوّبه، ثم طأطأ رأسه.

فلما رأت المرأة أنه لم يقض فيها شيئًا جلست، فقام رجل من أصحابه فقال: يا رسول الله، إن لم يكن لك بها حاجة فزوّجنيها.

فقال:

«هَلْ عِنْدَكَ شَيْءٌ؟»

قال: لا والله يا رسول الله.

قال:

«اذْهَبْ إِلَى أَهْلِكَ فَانْظُرْ هَلْ تَجِدُ شَيْئًا».

فذهب ثم رجع فقال: لا والله، ما وجدت شيئًا.

فقال رسول الله ﷺ:

«انْظُرْ وَلَوْ خَاتَمًا مِنْ حَدِيدٍ».

فذهب ثم رجع فقال: لا والله يا رسول الله، ولا خاتمًا من حديد، ولكن هذا إزاري - قال سهل: ما له رداء - فلها نصفه.

فقال رسول الله ﷺ:

«مَا تَصْنَعُ بِإِزَارِكَ؟ إِنْ لَبِسْتَهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْهَا مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ، وَإِنْ لَبِسَتْهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْكَ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ».

فجلس الرجل، حتى إذا طال مجلسه قام، فرآه رسول الله ﷺ مولّيًا، فأمر به فدعي له.

فلما جاء قال:

«مَا مَعَكَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ؟»

قال: معي سورة كذا وسورة كذا، عدّدها.

فقال:

«تَقْرَؤُهُنَّ عَنْ ظَهْرِ قَلْبٍ؟»

قال: نعم.

«اذْهَبْ، فَقَدْ مَلَّكْتُكَهَا بِمَا مَعَكَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ».

When he returned, he asked:

He replied:

“I know such-and-such surah and such-and-such surah,” and he listed them.

He replied:

“Yes.”

٦٥٠١ — عن أبي هريرة قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي ﷺ فقال: إني تزوجت امرأة من الأنصار. فقال له النبي ﷺ: (( هل نظرت إليها؟ فإن في عيون الأنصار شيئا )) قال: قد نظرت إليها. قال: (( على كم تزوجتها؟ )) قال: على أربع أواق، فقال له النبي ﷺ: (( على أربع أواق، كأنما تَنْحتون الفضة من عُرض هذا الجبل، ما عندنا ما نعطيك، ولكن عسى أن نبعثك في بعث تصيب منه )) قال: فبعث بعثاً إلى بني عبس، بعث ذلك الرجل فيهم.

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٧٥:١٤٢٤). وفيه كراهية إكثار المهر بالنسبة إلى حال الزوج.

english_source:
6501 — Abu Hurairah said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: I have married a woman from the Ansar. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Did you look at her? For indeed there is something in the eyes of the Ansar.” He said: I did look at her. He said: “For how much did you marry her?” He said: For four uqiyyahs. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: “For four uqiyyahs? It is as though you are carving silver from the side of this mountain. We do not have anything to give you, but perhaps we may send you on an expedition from which you may obtain something.” He said: Then he sent an expedition to Banu ʿAbs, and sent that man among them.

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1424 no. 75). In this is evidence for the dislike of an excessive dowry relative to the husband’s condition.

٦٥٠٤ — عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن أنه قال: سألت عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ كم كان صداق رسول الله ﷺ؟ قالت: كان صداقه لأزواجه ثنتي عشرة أوقيةً ونشًّا. قالت: أتدري ما النشّ؟ قال: قلت: لا. قالت: نصف أوقية، فتلك خمسمائة درهم، فهذا صداقُ رسول الله ﷺ لأزواجه.

٦٥٠٥ — عن أم حبيبة أنها كانت تحت عبيد الله بن جحش فمات بأرض الحبشة فزوّجها النجاشي النبيَّ ﷺ، وأمهرها عنه أربعة آلاف، وبعث بها إلى رسول الله ﷺ مع شرحبيل بن حسنة. ولم يبعث إليها رسول الله ﷺ بشيء، وكان مهر نسائه أربعمائة درهم.

قال أبو داود: حسنة هي أمه.

صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢١٠٧) والنسائي (٣٣٥٠) وأحمد (٢٧٤٠٨) والحاكم (١٨١/٢) والبيهقي (٢٣٢/٧).

6505 — Umm Habibah had been married to ʿUbayd Allah ibn Jahsh, and he died in the land of Abyssinia. Then the Negus married her to the Prophet ﷺ and gave her, on his behalf, a dowry of four thousand. He sent her to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with Sharhabil ibn Hasanah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not send her anything, while the dowries of his other wives were four hundred dirhams.

Abu Dawud said: Hasanah was his mother.

Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2107), al-Nasa’i (3350), Ahmad (27408), al-Hakim (2/181), and al-Bayhaqi (7/232).

٦٥٠٦ — عن أنس أن رسول الله ﷺغزا، فصلينا عندها صلاةَ الغداة بغلس، فركب نبي الله ﷺ وركب أبو طلحة، وأنا رديفُ أبي طلحة، فأجرى نبي الله ﷺ في زقاق خيبر، وإنَّ ركبتي لتمسُّ فخذ نبي الله ﷺ ثم حسَر الإزار عن فخذه، حتى إني أنظرُ إلى بياض فخذ نبي الله ﷺ فلما دخل القرية قال: (( الله أكبر خربتْ خيبر، إنا إذا نزلنا بساحة قومٍ، فساء صباحُ المنذرين)). قالها ثلاثا، قال: وخرج القومُ إلى أعمالهم، فقالوا: محمد - قال عبد العزيز، وقال بعض أصحابنا: والخميس، يعني الجيشَ - فأصبناها عَنْوةً، فجُمعَ السبيُ، فجاء دحيةُ، فقال: يا نبي الله، أعطني جارية من السبّي، قال: (( اذهبُ فخُذْ جاريةً)) فأخذ صفيةَ بنت حُيَيّ، فجاء رجل إلى النبي ﷺ فقال: يا نبي الله، أعطيتَ دحيةً صفية بنت حيي، سيدةَ قريظة والنضير؟ لا تَصلح إلا لك، قال: (( ادعُوه بها )) فجاء بها، فلما نظر إليها النبي ﷺ قال: (( خُذْ جاريةً من السبي غيرها)) قال: فأعتقها النبي ﷺ وتزوّجها. فقال له ثابت: يا أباحمزة، ما أصدقها؟ قال: نفسها، أعتقها وتزوّجها، حتى إذا كان بالطريق جهّزتْها له أمُّ سُليم، فأهدتها له من الليل، فأصبح النبي ﷺ عروساً فقال: (( من كان عنده شيء فليجيء به )) وبسط نِطْعا، فجعل الرجل يجيء بالأقِط، وجعل الرجل يجيء بالتمر، وجعل الرجل يجيء بالسمن، قال: وأحسبه قد ذكر السويق، قال: فحاسوا حيْسا، فكانتْ وليمة رسول الله ﷺ عليها

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٧١)، ومسلم (٨٤:١٣٦٥).

والحيس: هو نوع من الطعام يصنع من الأقط والتمر والسمن يخلط ويُعجن، وربما يخلط فيه أيضا السويق.

english_source:
6506 — Anas narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on a military expedition, and we prayed the dawn prayer there in the darkness before daylight. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ rode, and Abu Talhah rode, and I was riding behind Abu Talhah. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ urged his mount through the lanes of Khaybar, and my knee was touching the thigh of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ. Then he uncovered his thigh from his waist-wrapper until I could see the whiteness of the Prophet’s thigh. When he entered the town, he said, “Allah is the Greatest! Khaybar is ruined. When we descend in the courtyard of a people, evil is the morning of those who were warned.” He said this three times. The people had gone out to their work, and they said, “Muhammad!” ʿAbd al-ʿAziz said, and some of our companions said, “and the army,” meaning the army. So we conquered it by force, and the captives were gathered. Dihyah came and said, “O Prophet of Allah, give me a slave girl from the captives.” He said, “Go and take a slave girl.” So he took Safiyyah bint Huyayy. Then a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “O Prophet of Allah, you gave Dihyah Safiyyah bint Huyayy, the chief lady of Qurayzah and al-Nadir. She is suitable for no one but you.” He said, “Bring him with her.” So he brought her. When the Prophet ﷺ looked at her, he said, “Take another slave girl from the captives besides her.” Then the Prophet ﷺ freed her and married her. Thabit said to him: O Abu Hamzah, what did he give her as her dowry? He said: Her own self. He freed her and married her. Then when they were on the road, Umm Sulaym prepared her for him and sent her to him at night. By morning, the Prophet ﷺ was a bridegroom, and he said, “Whoever has anything, let him bring it.” He spread out a leather cloth, and one man brought dried curds, another brought dates, and another brought clarified butter. I think he also mentioned roasted flour. Then they mixed it into a dish of hays, and that was the wedding feast of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (371) and Muslim (1365 no. 84).

Al-hays is a type of food made from dried curds, dates, and clarified butter, mixed and kneaded together, and sometimes roasted flour is also mixed into it.

٦٥٠٦ — عن أنس أن رسول الله ﷺغزا، فصلينا عندها صلاةَ الغداة بغلس، فركب نبي الله ﷺ وركب أبو طلحة، وأنا رديفُ أبي طلحة، فأجرى نبي الله ﷺ في زقاق خيبر، وإنَّ ركبتي لتمسُّ فخذ نبي الله ﷺ ثم حسَر الإزار عن فخذه، حتى إني أنظرُ إلى بياض فخذ نبي الله ﷺ فلما دخل القرية قال: (( الله أكبر خربتْ خيبر، إنا إذا نزلنا بساحة قومٍ، فساء صباحُ المنذرين)). قالها ثلاثا، قال: وخرج القومُ إلى أعمالهم، فقالوا: محمد - قال عبد العزيز، وقال بعض أصحابنا: والخميس، يعني الجيشَ - فأصبناها عَنْوةً، فجُمعَ السبيُ، فجاء دحيةُ، فقال: يا نبي الله، أعطني جارية من السبّي، قال: (( اذهبُ فخُذْ جاريةً)) فأخذ صفيةَ بنت حُيَيّ، فجاء رجل إلى النبي ﷺ فقال: يا نبي الله، أعطيتَ دحيةً صفية بنت حيي، سيدةَ قريظة والنضير؟ لا تَصلح إلا لك، قال: (( ادعُوه بها )) فجاء بها، فلما نظر إليها النبي ﷺ قال: (( خُذْ جاريةً من السبي غيرها)) قال: فأعتقها النبي ﷺ وتزوّجها. فقال له ثابت: يا أباحمزة، ما أصدقها؟ قال: نفسها، أعتقها وتزوّجها، حتى إذا كان بالطريق جهّزتْها له أمُّ سُليم، فأهدتها له من الليل، فأصبح النبي ﷺ عروساً فقال: (( من كان عنده شيء فليجيء به )) وبسط نِطْعا، فجعل الرجل يجيء بالأقِط، وجعل الرجل يجيء بالتمر، وجعل الرجل يجيء بالسمن، قال: وأحسبه قد ذكر السويق، قال: فحاسوا حيْسا، فكانتْ وليمة رسول الله ﷺ عليها

٦٥٠٧ — عن أنس قال: صَارَتْ صَفِيَّهُ لِدِحْيَةَ فِي مَقْسَمِهِ، وَجَعَلُوا يَمْدَحُونَها عِنْدَ رَسُولِ الله ﷺ قَالَ: وَيَقُولُونَ مَا رَأَيْنَا فِي السَّبْي مِثْلَهَا، قَالَ: فَبَعَثَ إِلَى دِحْيَةَ فَأَعْطَاهُ بِهَا مَا أَرَادَ، ثُمَّ دَفَعَهَا إِلَى أُمِّي، فَقَالَ: ((أَصْلِحِيهَا)). قَالَ: ثُمَّ خَرَجَ رَسُولُ الله ﷺ مِنْ خَيْبَرَ حَتَّى إِذَا جَعَلَهَا فِي ظَهْرِهِ، نَزَلَ، ثُمَّ ضَرَبَ عَلَيْهَا الْقُبَّةَ، فَلَمَا أَصْبَحَ قَالَ رَسُولُ الله ﷺ: (( مَنْ كَانَ عِنْدَهُ فَضْلُ زَادٍ فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِهِ )). قَالَ: فَجَعَلَ الرَّجُلُ يَجِيءُ بِفَضْلِ التَّمْرِ وَفَضْلِ السَّوِيقِ حَتَّى جَعَلُوا مِنْ ذَلِكَ سَوَادًا حَيْسًا، فَجَعَلُوا يَأْكُلُونَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الحَيْسِ وَيَشْرَبُونَ مِنْ حِيَاضٍ إِلَى جَنْبِهِمْ مِنْ مَاءِ السَّمَاءِ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ أَنَسٌ: فَكَانَتْ تِلْكَ وَلِيمَةَ رَسُولِ الله ﷺ عَلَيْهَا، قَالَ: فَانْطَلَقْنَا حَتَّى إِذَا رَأَيْنَا جُدُرَ المدِينَةِ هَشِشْنَا إِلَيْهَا فَرَفَعْنَا مَطِيَّنَا وَرَفَعَ رَسُولُ الله ﷺ مَطِيَّتَهُ، قَالَ: وَصَفِيَّةُ خَلْفَهُ قَدْ أَرْدَفَهَا رَسُولُ الله ﷺ، قَالَ: فَعَثَرَتْ مَطِيَّةُ رَسُولِ الله ﷺ، فَصُرِعَ وَصُرِعَتْ، قَالَ: فَلَيْسَ أَحَدٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِ وَلا إِلَيْهَا حَتَّى قَامَ رَسُولُ الله ﷺ فَسَتَرَهَا، قَالَ: فَأَتَيْنَاهُ، فَقَالَ: (( لَمْ نُضَرَّ )). قَالَ: فَدَخَلْنَا المدِينَةَ، فَخَرَجَ جَوَارِي نِسَائِهِ يَتَرَاءَيْنَهَا وَيَشْمَتْنَ بِصَرْعَتِهَا.

صحيح: رواه مسلم في النكاح (٨٨ :١٣٦٥)

english_source:
6507 — Anas said: Safiyyah fell to Dihyah in his allotted share, and they began praising her before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: We have not seen anyone like her among the captives. So he sent for Dihyah and gave him in exchange what he wished, then he handed her over to my mother and said, “Prepare her.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left Khaybar, and when he placed her behind him on his mount, he stopped and set up a tent over her. When morning came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Whoever has extra provisions, let him bring them to us.” Then one man would bring extra dates, and another extra roasted flour, until they made from that a large amount of hays. They began eating from that hays and drinking from pools beside them filled with rainwater. Anas said: That was the wedding feast of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for her. Then we proceeded on until, when we saw the walls of Madinah, we became eager for it and hastened our mounts, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ also hastened his mount. Safiyyah was behind him, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had seated her behind him. Then the mount of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stumbled, and he fell and she fell. No one among the people looked at him or at her until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and covered her. Then we came to him, and he said, “We have not been harmed.” Then we entered Madinah, and the servant girls of his wives came out looking at her and gloating over her fall.

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Marriage (1365 no. 88).

٦٥٠٧ — عن أنس قال: صَارَتْ صَفِيَّهُ لِدِحْيَةَ فِي مَقْسَمِهِ، وَجَعَلُوا يَمْدَحُونَها عِنْدَ رَسُولِ الله ﷺ قَالَ: وَيَقُولُونَ مَا رَأَيْنَا فِي السَّبْي مِثْلَهَا، قَالَ: فَبَعَثَ إِلَى دِحْيَةَ فَأَعْطَاهُ بِهَا مَا أَرَادَ، ثُمَّ دَفَعَهَا إِلَى أُمِّي، فَقَالَ: ((أَصْلِحِيهَا)). قَالَ: ثُمَّ خَرَجَ رَسُولُ الله ﷺ مِنْ خَيْبَرَ حَتَّى إِذَا جَعَلَهَا فِي ظَهْرِهِ، نَزَلَ، ثُمَّ ضَرَبَ عَلَيْهَا الْقُبَّةَ، فَلَمَا أَصْبَحَ قَالَ رَسُولُ الله ﷺ: (( مَنْ كَانَ عِنْدَهُ فَضْلُ زَادٍ فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِهِ )). قَالَ: فَجَعَلَ الرَّجُلُ يَجِيءُ بِفَضْلِ التَّمْرِ وَفَضْلِ السَّوِيقِ حَتَّى جَعَلُوا مِنْ ذَلِكَ سَوَادًا حَيْسًا، فَجَعَلُوا يَأْكُلُونَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الحَيْسِ وَيَشْرَبُونَ مِنْ حِيَاضٍ إِلَى جَنْبِهِمْ مِنْ مَاءِ السَّمَاءِ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ أَنَسٌ: فَكَانَتْ تِلْكَ وَلِيمَةَ رَسُولِ الله ﷺ عَلَيْهَا، قَالَ: فَانْطَلَقْنَا حَتَّى إِذَا رَأَيْنَا جُدُرَ المدِينَةِ هَشِشْنَا إِلَيْهَا فَرَفَعْنَا مَطِيَّنَا وَرَفَعَ رَسُولُ الله ﷺ مَطِيَّتَهُ، قَالَ: وَصَفِيَّةُ خَلْفَهُ قَدْ أَرْدَفَهَا رَسُولُ الله ﷺ، قَالَ: فَعَثَرَتْ مَطِيَّةُ رَسُولِ الله ﷺ، فَصُرِعَ وَصُرِعَتْ، قَالَ: فَلَيْسَ أَحَدٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِ وَلا إِلَيْهَا حَتَّى قَامَ رَسُولُ الله ﷺ فَسَتَرَهَا، قَالَ: فَأَتَيْنَاهُ، فَقَالَ: (( لَمْ نُضَرَّ )). قَالَ: فَدَخَلْنَا المدِينَةَ، فَخَرَجَ جَوَارِي نِسَائِهِ يَتَرَاءَيْنَهَا وَيَشْمَتْنَ بِصَرْعَتِهَا.

صحيح: رواه مسلم في النكاح (٨٨ :١٣٦٥)

6507 — Anas said: Safiyyah fell to Dihyah in his allotted share, and they began praising her before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: We have not seen anyone like her among the captives. So he sent for Dihyah and gave him in exchange what he wished, then he handed her over to my mother and said, “Prepare her.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left Khaybar, and when he placed her behind him on his mount, he stopped and set up a tent over her. When morning came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Whoever has extra provisions, let him bring them to us.” Then one man would bring extra dates, and another extra roasted flour, until they made from that a large amount of hays. They began eating from that hays and drinking from pools beside them filled with rainwater. Anas said: That was the wedding feast of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for her. Then we proceeded on until, when we saw the walls of Madinah, we became eager for it and hastened our mounts, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ also hastened his mount. Safiyyah was behind him, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had seated her behind him. Then the mount of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stumbled, and he fell and she fell. No one among the people looked at him or at her until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and covered her. Then we came to him, and he said, “We have not been harmed.” Then we entered Madinah, and the servant girls of his wives came out looking at her and gloating over her fall.

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Marriage (1365 no. 88).

٦٥٠٨ — عن جويرية بنت الحارث قالت لرسول الله ﷺ إن أزواجك يفخرن عليّ، يقلن: لم يتزوجك رسول الله ﷺ إنما أنت ملك يمين. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: (( ألم أعظم صداقك، ألم أعتق أربعين من قومك )).

صحيح: رواه إسحاق في مسنده (٢٥٥/٤) وعبد الرزاق (٢٧٢-٢٧١/٧) والحاكم (٢٥/٤).

6508 — Juwayriyyah bint al-Harith said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Your wives boast over me and say: The Messenger of Allah did not really marry you; you are only a bondwoman. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Did I not make your dowry great? Did I not free forty of your people?”

Authentic: Narrated by Ishaq in his Musnad (4/255), ʿAbd al-Razzaq (7/271–272), and al-Hakim (4/25).

٦٥٠٩ — عن أبي موسى قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: (( ثلاثة لهم أجران)) منهم: (( رجل كانت عنده أمةٌ فأدّبَها فأحسن تأديبها، وعلّمها فأحسن تعليمها، ثم أعتَقها، فتزوَّجها، فله أجران ))

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري في العلم (٩٧) ومسلم في الإيمان (١٥٤). وقوله: “فتزوّجها”: أي بالمهر.

english_source:
6509 — Abu Musa said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Three people will have a double reward.” Among them is: “A man who had a slave woman, disciplined her and did so well, taught her and taught her well, then freed her and married her — he will have two rewards.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Knowledge (97) and Muslim in the Book of Faith (154).

His statement, “then married her,” means with a dowry.

٦٥١٠ — عن عائشة قالت: أتتْ جويريةُ بنت الحارث رسولَ الله ﷺ تستعينه في كتابتها، فو الله ما هو إلا أن وقفتْ على باب الحجرة، فرأيتها فكرهتُ مكانها، وعرفتُ أن رسول الله ﷺ سيرى منها مثل ما رأيتُ. فقالت جويرية: يا رسول الله ﷺ كان من الأمر ما قد عرفت، فكاتبت نفسي فجئت أستعينك. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: (( أو ما هو خير من ذلك؟ )) قالت: ما هو؟ قال: (( أتزوّجكِ وأقضي عنكِ كتابتكِ )) فقالت: نعم. قال: (( قد فعلتُ )). قالت: فبلغ المسلمين ذلك فقالوا: أصهار رسول الله ﷺ، فأرسلوا ما كان في أيديهم من سبايا بني المصطلق. قالت: فلقد عُتق بتزويجه مائة أهل بيت من بني المصطلق. قالت: فما أعلم امرأة كانت أعظم بركة على قومها منها.

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٩٣١) وأحمد (٢٦٣٦٥) وابن حبان (٤٠٥٤) والحاكم (٢٦/٤).

6510 — ʿA’ishah said: Juwayriyyah bint al-Harith came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seeking his help regarding her emancipation contract. By Allah, as soon as she stood at the door of the room, I saw her and disliked her place there, for I knew that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would see in her what I had seen. Juwayriyyah said: O Messenger of Allah, you know what has happened to me. I made a contract for my freedom, and I have come seeking your help. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Shall I not offer you something better than that?” She said: What is it? He said, “I will marry you and pay off your contract for you.” She said: Yes. He said: “I have done so.” She said: When the Muslims heard that, they said: They are the relatives by marriage of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So they released whatever captives of Banu al-Mustaliq were in their hands. She said: One hundred households of Banu al-Mustaliq were freed because of his marriage to her. She said: I do not know of any woman who brought a greater blessing upon her people than she did.

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3931), Ahmad (26365), Ibn Hibban (4054), and al-Hakim (4/26).

٦٥١٢ — عن عائشة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: (( إن من يُمنِ المرأة تيسيرُ خِطبتها، وتيسيرُ صداقِها، وتيسيرُ رحمِها )).

حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٤٤٧٨) والبزار - كشف الأستار (١٤١٧) وابن حبان (٤٠٩٥) والحاكم (١٨١/٢).

Hasan: Narrated by Ahmad (24478), al-Bazzar in Kashf al-Astar (1417), Ibn Hibban (4095), and al-Hakim (2/181).

٦٥١٣ — عن أبي العَجْفاء السُّلمي قال: خطبنا عمر فقال: ألا لا تغالوا بصُدق النساء، فإنها لو كانت مكرمةً في الدنيا، أو تقوى عند الله كان أولاكم بها النبي ﷺ. ما أصدق رسولُ الله ﷺ امرأة من نسائه، ولا أُصدِقتْ امرأةٌ من بناته أكثر من ثنتي عشرة أوقية.

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢١٠٦) والنسائي (٣٣٤٩) والترمذي (١١١٤) وابن ماجه (١٨٨٧) وأحمد (٣٤٠).

english_source:
6513 — Abu al-ʿAjfa’ al-Sulami said: ʿUmar addressed us and said: Do not be excessive in the dowries of women, for if that were an honor in this world or a sign of piety before Allah, then the Prophet ﷺ would have been more entitled to it than you. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not give any of his wives as dowry, nor was any of his daughters given in marriage for more than twelve uqiyyahs.

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2106), al-Nasa’i (3349), al-Tirmidhi (1114), Ibn Majah (1887), and Ahmad (340).

٦٥١٤ — عن عقبة بن عامر أن النبي ﷺ قال لرجل: (( أترضى أن أزوجك فلانة؟ )) قال: نعم، وقال للمرأة: (( أترضين أن أزوجك فلاناً؟ )) قالت: نعم، فزوج أحدهما صاحبه، فدخل بها الرجل، ولم يفرض لها صداقاً، ولم يعطها شيئاً. وكان ممن شهد الحديبية له سهم خيبر. فلما حضرتُه الوفاةُ قال: إن رسول الله ﷺ زوجني فلانة، ولم أفرض لها صداقاً، ولم أُعطها شيئاً، وإني أُشْهِدكم أني أعطيتُها من صداقها سهْمي بخيبر، فأخذتْ سهماً فباعته بمائة ألف.

صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢١١٧) وصحّحه ابن حبان (٤٠٧٢) والحاكم (١٨٢-١٨١/٢).

6514 — ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said to a man, “Are you pleased that I marry so-and-so to you?” He said: Yes. And he said to the woman, “Are you pleased that I marry so-and-so to you?” She said: Yes. So he married one of them to the other. The man consummated the marriage with her, but he had not specified any dowry for her and had not given her anything. He was among those who had witnessed al-Hudaybiyah and thus had a share from Khaybar. When death approached him, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married me to so-and-so, and I did not specify any dowry for her, nor did I give her anything. I make you witnesses that I have given her my share from Khaybar as her dowry. So she took the share and sold it for one hundred thousand.

Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2117), and authenticated by Ibn Hibban (4072) and al-Hakim (2/181–182).

٦٥١٥ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود في رجل تزوج امرأةً فمات عنها، ولم يَدخُل بها، ولم يَفْرِضُ لها الصداقَ. فقال: لها الصداقُ كاملاً، وعليها العدة، ولها الميراث.

قال معقل بن سنان: سمعتُ رسول الله ﷺ قضى في بروَع بنت واشق.

صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢١١٤) والنسائي (٣٣٥٦) وابن ماجه (١٨٩١) وصحّحه ابن حبان.

english_source:
6515 — ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud gave judgment concerning a man who married a woman and then died before consummating the marriage and before specifying a dowry for her. He said: She is entitled to the full dowry, she must observe the waiting period, and she is entitled to inheritance. Maʿqil ibn Sinan said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ give judgment concerning Barwaʿ bint Washiq in that way.

Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2114), al-Nasa’i (3356), Ibn Majah (1891), and authenticated by Ibn Hibban.

٦٥١٦ — عن عروة بن الزبير يحدث أنه سأل عائشة: (وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا تُقْسِطُوا فِى الْيَتَمَىٰ فَانكِحُواْ مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ) [النساء: ٣] قالت: هي اليتيمة في حجر وليها، فيرغب في جمالها ومالها ويريد أن يتزوجها بأدنى من سنة نسائها، فنهوا عن نكاحهن، إلا أن يُقسطوا لهن في إكمال الصداق، وأمروا بنكاح من سواهن من النساء.

قالت عائشة: ثم استفتى الناس رسول الله ﷺ بعدُ، فأنزل الله عز وجل: (وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ فِي النِّسَاءِ قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ) [النساء: ١٢٧] قالت: فبيَّن الله في هذه أن اليتيمة إذا كانت ذات جمال ومال، رغبوا في نكاحها، ولم يُلحقوها بسنتها في إكمال الصداق، فإذا كانت مرغوباً عنها في قلة المال والجمال تركوها، والتمسوا غيرها من النساء. قال: فكما يتركونها حين يرغبون عنها، فليس لهم أن ينكحوها إذا رغبوا فيها إلا أن يُقسطوا لها الأوفى من الصداق، ويُعطوها حقها.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٧٦٣) ومسلم (٦:٣٠١٨). واللفظ للبخاري.

6516 — ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated that he asked ʿA’ishah about the verse: “And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry those women who seem good to you” [al-Nisa’ 4:3]. She said: This refers to an orphan girl under the care of her guardian. He may be attracted to her beauty and wealth and want to marry her for less than the dowry normally given to women like her. So they were forbidden from marrying such girls unless they deal justly with them by giving them the full dowry, and they were instructed to marry other women besides them.

ʿA’ishah said: Then the people sought a ruling from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ after that, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: “And they ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning them” [al-Nisa’ 4:127]. She said: Allah made clear in this verse that when the orphan girl possessed beauty and wealth, they desired to marry her, but they would not give her what women like her deserved in full dowry. Yet when she was not desired because of little wealth or beauty, they would leave her and seek other women instead. So just as they leave her when they have no desire for her, they have no right to marry her when they do desire her unless they are fully just with her in the dowry and give her her due.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2763) and Muslim (3018 no. 6). The wording is that of al-Bukhari.

٦٥١٧ — عن أنس بن مالك، أن عبد الرحمن بن عوف جاء إلى رسول الله ﷺ وبه أثر صفرة، فسأله رسول الله ﷺ فأخبره أنه تزوج. فقال له رسول الله ﷺ: (( كم سُقت إليها؟ )) فقال: زنة نواة من ذهب. فقال له رسول الله ﷺ: (( أولِمْ ولو بشاةٍ ))

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٤٧) والبخاري (٥١٥٣) ومسلم (٨١:١٤٢٧). وقوله: (( كم سُقْتَ إليها )): أي ما أمهرتها، وقيل للمهر: سوق؛ لأن العرب كانت أموالهم المواشي، فكان الرجلُ إذا تزوج ساق إليها الإبل والغنم مهراً.

وفي الحديث رخصة في استعمال الصفرة من الزعفران وغيره للعريس.

english_source:
6517 — Anas ibn Malik narrated that ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a trace of yellow perfume on him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him, and he informed him that he had married. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, “What did you give her?” He said: The weight of a date-stone of gold. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, “Give a wedding feast, even if only with one sheep.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (47), al-Bukhari (5153), and Muslim (1427 no. 81).

His statement, “What did you bring to her?” means: What did you give as her dowry? The dowry was called “bringing” because the Arabs’ wealth was mostly livestock, so when a man married, he would bring camels or sheep to her as dowry.

In this hadith is a concession for the bridegroom to use yellow coloring from saffron and similar things.

٦٥١٨ — عن عبد الرَّحْمَنِ بِن عَوْفٍ قَالَ: لما قَدِمْنَا المدِينَةَ آخَى رَسُولُ الله ﷺ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ سَعْدِ بْنِ الرَّبِيعِ، فَقَالَ سَعْدُ بْنُ الرَّبِيعِ: إِنِّي أَكْثَرُ الْأَنْصَارِ مَالاً، فَأَقْسِمُ لَكَ نِصْفَ مَالِي، وَانْظُرْ أَيَّ زَوْجَتَيَّ هَوِيتَ، نَزَلْتُ لَكَ عَنْهَا، فَإِذَا حَلَّتْ تَزَوَّجْتَهَا. قَالَ: فَقَالَ لَهُ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ: لَا حَاجَةَ لِي فِي ذَلِكَ، هَلْ مِنْ سُوقٍ فِيهِ تِجَارَةٌ؟ قَالَ: سُوقُ قَيْنُقَاعَ. قَالَ: فَغَدَا إِلَيْهِ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ، فَأَتَى بِأَقِطٍ وَسَمْنٍ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ تَابَعَ الغُدُوَّ، فَمَا لَبِثَ أَنْ جَاءَ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ عَلَيْهِ أَثَرُ صُفْرَةٍ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ الله ﷺ: (( تَزَوَّجْتَ؟ )) قَالَ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ: (( وَمَنْ؟ )) قَالَ: امْرَأَةً مِنَ الْأَنْصَارِ. قَالَ: (( كَمْ سُقْتَ؟ )) قَالَ: زِنَةَ نَوَاةٍ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ أَوْ نَوَاةً مِنْ ذَهَبٍ. فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: (( أَوْلِمْ وَلَوْ بِشَاةٍ )).

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٠٤٨).

6518 — ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf said: When we came to Madinah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established brotherhood between me and Saʿd ibn al-Rabiʿ. So the Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Give a wedding feast, even if only with one sheep.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2048).

٦٥١٩ — عن ثابت قال: ذُكرَ تزويجُ زينب بنت جحش عند أنس، فقال: ما رأيتُ النبي ﷺ أولمَ على أحد من نسائه ما أولمَ عليها، أولمَ بشاة.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥١٧١) ومسلم (٩٠:١٤٢٨). واللفظ للبخاري.

وفي لفظ مسلم: ما أولَم رسول الله ﷺ على امرأة من نسائه أكثرَ وأفضلَ مما أولَم على زينب. فقال ثابت للبناني: بما أولَم؟ قال: “أطعمهم خبزاً ولحماً حتى تركوه”. وتفصيله عند البخاري (٤٧٩٣) قال: بُني على النبي ﷺ بزينب بخبز ولحم، فأرسلتُ على الطعام داعياً، فيجيء قوم فيأكلون ويخرجون، ثم يجيء قوم فيأكلون ويخرجون. فدعوتُ حتى ما أجد أحداً أدعوه. فقلت: يا نبي الله ما أجد أحداً أدعوه. قال: (( ارفعوا طعامكم )).

english_source:
6519 — Thabit said: The marriage of Zaynab bint Jahsh was mentioned in the presence of Anas, and he said: I did not see the Prophet ﷺ give a wedding feast for any of his wives as he did for her. He gave a feast with one sheep.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5171) and Muslim (1428 no. 90). The wording is that of al-Bukhari.

In the wording of Muslim: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not give a larger or better wedding feast for any of his wives than the one he gave for Zaynab. Thabit al-Bunani asked: With what did he give the feast? He said: He fed them bread and meat until they left it. Its detail in al-Bukhari (4793) is: The Prophet ﷺ consummated his marriage with Zaynab, and bread and meat were served. I went calling people to the food. A group would come, eat, and leave; then another group would come, eat, and leave. I continued inviting until I could no longer find anyone to invite. So I said: O Prophet of Allah, I cannot find anyone else to invite. He said: “Remove your food.”

٦٥٢٢ — عن أنس قال: تزوج النبي ﷺ صفية، وجعل عتقها صداقها، وجعل الوليمة ثلاثة أيام، وبسط نطعا جاءت به أم سُليم، وألقى عليه أقطا وتمرا، وأطعم الناس ثلاثة أيام.

حسن: رواه أبو يعلى (٣٨٣٤).

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Yaʿla (3834).

٦٥٢٣ — عن أنس قال: أقام النبي ﷺ بين خيبر والمدينة ثلاثا، يُبنى عليه بصفية بنت حيي. فدعوتُ المسلمين إلى وليمته، فما كان فيها من خبز ولا لحم، أمر بالأنطاع، فألقى فيها من التمر والأقط والسمن، فكانت وليمته.

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥٠٨٥).

6523 — Anas said: The Prophet ﷺ stayed between Khaybar and Madinah for three days while consummating his marriage to Safiyyah bint Huyayy. I invited the Muslims to his wedding feast. There was neither bread nor meat in it. He ordered that leather cloths be spread, then dates, dried curds, and clarified butter were placed on them, and that was his wedding feast.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5085).

٦٥٢٤ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: أعتق النبي ﷺ صفية بنت حيي سيدة قريظة والنضير، وتزوجها فأصبح عرُوسا فقال: (( من كان عنده شيء فليجيء به)). قال: وبسط نِطْعاً قال: فجعل الرجل يجيء بالأقط، وجعل الرجل يجيء بالتمر، وجعل الرجل يجيء بالسمن فحاسوا حيسا. فكانت وليمة رسول الله ﷺ.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٧١) ومسلم (٨٤:١٣٦٥).

6524 — Anas ibn Malik said: The Prophet ﷺ freed Safiyyah bint Huyayy, the chief lady of Qurayzah and al-Nadir, and married her. In the morning, when he was a bridegroom, he said, “Whoever has anything, let him bring it.” He spread out a leather mat, and one man brought dried curds, another brought dates, and another brought clarified butter, and they mixed it into hays. That was the wedding feast of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (371) and Muslim (1365 no. 84).

٦٥٢٦ — عن ابن عمر، أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: (( إذا دعي أحدكم إلى وليمةِ فليأتِها)).

وفي لفظ: (( إذا دعي أحدكم إلى وليمة عُرس فليُجِبْ))

وفي آخر: (( إذا دعا أحدُكم أخاه فليُجِبْ عُرسا كان أو نحوه)).

صحيح: رواه مالك (٤٩) والبخاري (٥١٧٣)، ومسلم (٩٦:١٤٢٩).

6526 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “If one of you is invited to a wedding feast, let him attend it.”

In another wording: “If one of you is invited to a wedding feast, let him respond.”

And in another: “When one of you invites his brother, let him accept, whether it is for a wedding or something similar.”

Authentic: Narrated by Malik (49), al-Bukhari (5173), and Muslim (1429 no. 96).

٦٥٢٧ — عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: (( أجيبوا هذه الدعوة إذا دعيتم لها)).

قال: كان عبد الله يأتي الدعوة في العُرس وغير العُرس وهو صائم.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥١٧٩)، ومسلم (١٠٣:١٤٢٩).

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5179) and Muslim (1429 no. 103).

٦٥٣١ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: أبصر النبي ﷺ نساءً وصبيانًا مقبلين من عرس، فقام ممتنا، فقال: (( اللهم أنتم من أحب الناس إلي )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥١٨٠) ومسلم (١٧٤:٢٥٠٨).

قوله: (( فقام ممتنا )) أي من الامتنان، فمن قام له النبيُّ ﷺ وأكرمه بذلك فقد امتنّ عليه بشيء لا أعظم منه.

6531 — Anas ibn Malik said: The Prophet ﷺ saw women and children coming from a wedding, so he stood up in honor and said, “By Allah, you are among the most beloved people to me.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5180) and Muslim (2508 no. 174).

His statement, “he stood up in honor,” means out of esteem and graciousness. Whoever the Prophet ﷺ stood for and honored in this way was honored with something beyond compare.

٦٥٣٢ — عن أبي مسعود الأنصاري قال:

جاء رجل من الأنصار يكنى أبا شعيب، فقال لغلام له قصاب - وفي رواية: لحام -:

اجعل لي طعامًا يكفي خمسة، فإني أريد أن أدعو النبي ﷺ خامس خمسة، فإني قد عرفت في وجهه الجوع.

فدعاهم، فجاء معهم رجل.

فقال النبي ﷺ:

«إِنَّ هَذَا قَدْ تَبِعَنَا، فَإِنْ شِئْتَ أَنْ تَأْذَنَ لَهُ فَأْذَنْ لَهُ، وَإِنْ شِئْتَ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ رَجَعَ».

فقال:

لا، بل قد أذنت له.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٠٨١)، ومسلم (٢٠٣٦).

6532 — Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī reported:

A man from the Anṣār known as Abū Shuʿayb said to a servant of his who was a butcher—and in another narration, a meat seller:

“Prepare food for me sufficient for five people, for I wish to invite the Prophet ﷺ as one of five, because I have noticed hunger in his face.”

He invited them, and another man came along with them.

The Prophet ﷺ said:

“This man has followed us. If you wish, you may give him permission to enter; and if you wish, he may return.”

The host replied:

“No, rather I give him permission.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2081) and Muslim (2036).

٦٥٣٣ — عن سهل قال:

لما عرّس أبو أسيد الساعدي، دعا النبي ﷺ وأصحابه، فما صنع لهم طعامًا، ولا قرّبه إليهم إلا امرأته أم أسيد.

بلّت تمرات في تور من حجارة من الليل، فلما فرغ النبي ﷺ من الطعام أماثته له، فسقته، تتحفه بذلك.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥١٨٢)، ومسلم (٢٠٠٦/٨٧). 

قوله: «أماثته» من ماثه وأماثه - ثلاثيًا ورباعيًا - أي أذابه.

وقوله: «تتحفه» من الإتحاف، وهو إعطاء التحفة.

6533 — Sahl reported:

When Abū Usayd al-Sāʿidī got married, he invited the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions.

No one prepared food for them or served it to them except his wife, Umm Usayd.

She had soaked some dates overnight in a stone vessel. When the Prophet ﷺ finished eating, she dissolved and mixed them for him, then gave it to him to drink as a special offering.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5182) and Muslim (2006/87). 

The word “amāthathu” means that she dissolved or thoroughly mixed it.

The expression “tuḥtifuhu” means that she presented it to him as a special gift or offering.

The expression “tuḥtifuhu” means that she presented it to him as a special gift or offering.

٦٥٣٤ — عن علي قال: صنعتُ طعاماً، فدعوت النبي ﷺ فجاء، فدخل فرأى ستراً، فيه تصاوير فرجع. قال: فقلت: يا رسول الله! ما رجعك بأبي أنت وأمي؟ قال: (( إن في البيتِ ستراً فيه تصاوير، وإن الملائكةَ لا تدخل بيتا فيه تصاوير )).

٦٥٣٥ — عن سفينة أبي عبد الرحمن، أن رجلا أضاف عليّ بن أبي طالب، فصنع له طعاماً. فقالتْ فاطمةُ: لو دعونا النبي ﷺ فأكل معنا. فدعوه فجاء، فوضع يده على عضادتي الباب، فرأى قراماً في ناحية البيت فرجع. فقالت فاطمة لعلي: الحق فقل له: ما رجعك؟ يا رسول الله! قال: (( إنه ليس لي أن أدخل بيتا مزوقا )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٧٥٥) وابن ماجه (٣٣٦٠) وصحّحه ابن حبان (٦٣٤٥) والحاكم (١٨٦/٢).

والقرام: الستر الرقيم. والمزوق: النقش.

english_source:
6535 — Safinah Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated that a man hosted ʿAli ibn Abi Talib and prepared food for him. Fatimah said: If only we would invite the Prophet ﷺ to eat with us. So they invited him, and he came. He placed his hand on the side-posts of the door, then saw a decorated curtain in one part of the house and turned back. Fatimah said to ʿAli: Go after him and ask him, O Messenger of Allah, what made you return? He said, “It is not for me to enter a decorated house.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3755), Ibn Majah (3360), and authenticated by Ibn Hibban (6345) and al-Hakim (2/186).

Al-qiram means a patterned curtain, and al-muzawwaq means adorned or decorated.

٦٥٣٦ — عن محمد بن حاطب قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ (( فصلٌ بين الحلال والحرام: الدفُّ والصوتُ في النكاح )).

حسن: رواه الترمذي (١٠٨٨) وحسّنه، والنسائي (٣٣٦٩) وابن ماجه (١٨٩٦) وصحّحه الحاكم (١٨٤/٢).

6536 — Muhammad ibn Hatib said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “What distinguishes the lawful from the unlawful is the beating of the drum and the raising of the voice in marriage.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (1088), who graded it Hasan, al-Nasa’i (3369), Ibn Majah (1896), and authenticated by al-Hakim (2/184).

٦٥٣٧ — عن الرُّبَيع بنت معوذ بن عفراء قالت: جاء النبي ﷺ فدخل حين بُنيَ عليّ، فجلس على فراشي كمجلسك مني. فجعلتْ جويريات لنا يضربن بالدف، ويندُبْنَ من قُتِلَ من آبائي يوم بدر، إذ قالت إحداهن: وفينا نبي يعلم ما في غد. فقال النبي ﷺ (( دعي هذه، وقولي بالذي كنتِ تقُولين )).

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥١٤٧).

6537 — Al-Rubayyiʿ bint Muʿawwidh ibn ʿAfra’ said: The Prophet ﷺ came and entered when my marriage was consummated, and he sat on my bedding as you are sitting near me. Then some young girls of ours began beating the duff and singing elegies for those of my forefathers who had been killed at Badr, until one of them said: “And among us is a Prophet who knows what will happen tomorrow.” The Prophet ﷺ said, “Leave this and say what you were saying before.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5147).

٦٥٣٩ — عن عائشة قالت: إن النبي ﷺ سمع أناسا يُغنُّون في عُرْسٍ، وهم يقولون:

وأهدى

لها أكبشا

تُبَحْبَحُ في

المربدِ

وزوجك في النادي

ويعلم ما

في غدِ

فقال النبي ﷺ: (( لا يعلم ما في غد إلا الله عز وجل )).

حسن: رواه الطبراني في الصغير (٣٤٣) والحاكم (١٨٦-١٧٥/٢) والبيهقي (٢٨٩/٧).

6539 — ʿA’ishah said: The Prophet ﷺ heard some people singing at a wedding, saying:

“He gave her some rams,

that frolic in the pen,

and your husband is in the gathering,

and knows what is in tomorrow.”

So the Prophet ﷺ said, “No one knows what is in tomorrow except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Saghir (343), al-Hakim (2/175–186), and al-Bayhaqi (7/289).

٦٥٣٩ — عن عائشة قالت: إن النبي ﷺ سمع أناسا يُغنُّون في عُرْسٍ، وهم يقولون:

وأهدى

لها أكبشا

تُبَحْبَحُ في

المربدِ

وزوجك في النادي

ويعلم ما

في غدِ

6541 — Jabir said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿA’ishah, “Have you escorted the young bride to her home?” She said: Yes. He said, “Why did you not send with her some who would sing, saying:

‘We have come to you, we have come to you,

so greet us and we will greet you,

for the Ansar are a people among whom there is love poetry.’”

Hasan: Narrated by Ahmad (15209) and al-Bazzar in Kashf al-Astar (1432).

٦٥٤٢ — عن عامر بن سعد البجلي يقول: شهدت ثابت بن وديعة وقرظة بن كعب الأنصاري في عرس، وإذا غناء، فقلت لهما في ذلك فقالا: إنه رُخّصَ في الغناء في العُرس، والبكاء على الميت في غير نياحة.

صحيح: رواه أبو داود الطيالسي (١٣١٧) والبيهقي (٢٨٩/٧).

6542 — ʿAmir ibn Saʿd al-Bajali said: I was present with Thabit ibn Wadiʿah and Qurzah ibn Kaʿb al-Ansari at a wedding, and there was singing. I spoke to them about that, and they said: Singing has been permitted at weddings, and weeping for the dead without wailing.

Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi (1317) and al-Bayhaqi (7/289).

٦٥٤٣ — عن عقبة بن عامر أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: (( إياكم والدخولَ على النساء )). فقال: رجل من الأنصار: يا رسول الله ﷺ أفرأيت الحمو؟ قال: (( الحموُ موتٌ )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٢٣٢) ومسلم (٢١٧٢). والحمْوُ: على وزن الدَلْو، قال النووي: “والمراد بالحمو هنا أقارب الزوج غير آبائه وأبنائه، فأما الآباء والأبناء فمحارم لزوجته، تجوز لهم الخلوة بها ولا يوصفون بالموت، وإنما المراد هو: الأخ وابن الأخ والعم وابنه ونحوهم ممن ليس بمحرم” اه.

english_source:
6543 — ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Beware of entering upon women.” A man from the Ansar said: O Messenger of Allah, what about the in-law? He said, “The in-law is death.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5232) and Muslim (2172).

Al-hamw means the husband’s male relatives other than his fathers and sons. Al-Nawawi said: What is meant here are the husband’s relatives other than his fathers and sons. As for fathers and sons, they are unmarriageable kin to the wife, and seclusion with them is permissible, so they are not described as “death.” Rather, what is meant is the brother, the brother’s son, the uncle, the uncle’s son, and the like among those who are not unmarriageable kin.

٦٥٤٥ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: (( ما منكم من أحد إلا وقد وُكِّل به قرينُه من الجن )). قالوا: وإياك يا رسول الله؟ قال: (( وإياي إلا أن الله أعانني عليه فأسلم فلا يأمرني إلا بخير )).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٨١٤). فقوله: “أسلم” من الإسلام دون السلامة هذا الذي فسر به جمهور العلماء هذا الحديث إلا سفيان بن عيينة فإنه فسره بقوله: أسلم - أي أجد منه السلامة. يعني أن النبي ﷺ سالم من أن يجري الشيطان فيه مجرى الدم، وهذا لا يشاركه فيه غيره.

٦٥٤٥ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: (( ما منكم من أحد إلا وقد وُكِّل به قرينُه من الجن )). قالوا: وإياك يا رسول الله؟ قال: (( وإياي إلا أن الله أعانني عليه فأسلم فلا يأمرني إلا بخير )).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٨١٤). فقوله: “أسلم” من الإسلام دون السلامة هذا الذي فسر به جمهور العلماء هذا الحديث إلا سفيان بن عيينة فإنه فسره بقوله: أسلم - أي أجد منه السلامة. يعني أن النبي ﷺ سالم من أن يجري الشيطان فيه مجرى الدم، وهذا لا يشاركه فيه غيره.
english_source:
6545 — ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “There is none among you except that his companion from among the jinn has been assigned to him.” They said: Even you, O Messenger of Allah? He said, “Even me, except that Allah helped me against him and he accepted Islam, so he does not command me except with good.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2814).

His statement, “he accepted Islam,” is understood by the majority of scholars literally as Islam, not merely safety. Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah explained it as “I am safe from him,” meaning the Prophet ﷺ was protected from Satan flowing through him like blood, and no one shares that with him.

٦٥٤٦ — عن ابن عباس يقول: سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول: (( ألا لا يخلونَّ رجل بامرأةٍ، إلا ومعها ذو محرم )).

متفق عليه: رواه مسلم (١٣٤١) والبخاري (٣٠٠٦)، واللفظ لمسلم.

٦٥٤٧ — عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص أن نفرا من بني هاشم دخلوا على أسماء بنت عميس، فدخل أبو بكر الصديق، وهي تحته يومئذ، فرآهم. فكره ذلك. فذكر ذلك للنبي ﷺ وقال: لم أر إلا خيراً فقال رسول الله ﷺ (( إن الله قد برأها من ذلك )). ثم قام رسول الله ﷺ على المنبر فقال: (( لا يدخلنَّ رجلٌ بعد يومي هذا على مغيبة إلا ومعه رجل أو اثنان )).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢١٧٣).

6547 — ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs narrated that a group from Banu Hashim entered upon Asma’ bint ʿUmays. Then Abu Bakr al-Siddiq entered, and she was his wife at that time, and he saw them and disliked that. He mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ and said: I saw nothing but good. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Allah has declared her free of that.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood upon the pulpit and said, “No man is to enter upon a woman whose husband is absent after this day unless he is accompanied by one or two men.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2173).

٦٥٤٨ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده، قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ (( أيما امرأةٍ نكحت على صداقٍ أو حِباء، أو عِدة قبل عصمة النكاح فهو لها، وما كان بعد عصمة النكاح فهو لمن أُعطيه، وأحق ما أُكرِمَ عليه الرجلُ ابنتُه أو أختُه )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢١٢٩) وابن ماجه (١٩٥٥) والنسائي (٣٣٥٣) وأحمد (٦٧٠٩).

6548 — ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Any woman who is married upon a dowry, or a gift, or a promise before the marriage bond is concluded, then it belongs to her. Whatever is given after the marriage bond is concluded belongs to the one to whom it is given. And the one most deserving that a man be honored through is his daughter or his sister.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2129), Ibn Majah (1955), al-Nasa’i (3353), and Ahmad (6709).

٦٥٥٠ — عن جابر قال: قال لي رسولُ الله ﷺ: (( هل لكم أنماط؟ )). قلت: وأنى يكون لنا الأنماط؟ قال: (( أما أنه سيكون لكم الأنماط )).

قال جابر: فأنا أقول لها - يعني امرأته - أخّري عني أنماطكِ، فتقول: ألم يقل النبي ﷺ: (( إنها ستكونُ لكم الأنماط؟ )) فأدعُها.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٦٣١) ومسلم (٢٠٨٣). واللفظ للبخاري. وقوله: (( الأنماط )): هو ضرب من البسط له حمل رقيق، يستعمل في الغالب في ليلة الزفاف، وفي الليالي التي تليها لاستقبال العروس.

english_source:
6550 — Jabir said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me, “Do you have carpets?” I said: How could we have carpets? He said, “But you will indeed have carpets.” Jabir said: So I say to her — meaning his wife — “Keep your carpets away from me,” and she says: Did not the Prophet ﷺ say, “You will indeed have carpets”? So I leave her alone.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3631) and Muslim (2083), and the wording is that of al-Bukhari.

Al-anmat are a kind of carpet or mat with a thin layer, generally used on the wedding night and the nights after it to receive the bride.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٦٣١) ومسلم (٢٠٨٣). واللفظ للبخاري. وقوله: (( الأنماط )): هو ضرب من البسط له حمل رقيق، يستعمل في الغالب في ليلة الزفاف، وفي الليالي التي تليها لاستقبال العروس.

6550 — Jabir said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me, “Do you have carpets?” I said: How could we have carpets? He said, “But you will indeed have carpets.” Jabir said: So I say to her — meaning his wife — “Keep your carpets away from me,” and she says: Did not the Prophet ﷺ say, “You will indeed have carpets”? So I leave her alone.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3631) and Muslim (2083), and the wording is that of al-Bukhari.

Al-anmat are a kind of carpet or mat with a thin layer, generally used on the wedding night and the nights after it to receive the bride.

٦٢١١ — عن أبي هريرة أن أبا هند حجم النبي ﷺ في اليافوخ، فقال له النبي ﷺ: (( يا بني بياضة، أنكحوا أبا هند، أنكحوا إليه )). وقال: (( وإن كان في شيء مما تداوون به خير فالحجامة )). وفي رواية: (( كان حجاماً )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢١٠٢)، والدارقطني (٣/٣٠٠-٣٠١)، وابن حبان (٤٠٦٧)، والحاكم (٢/١٦٤).

وقوله: (( وأنكحوا إليه )) أي اخطبوا إليه بناته.

english_source:
6211 — Abu Hurayrah reported that Abu Hind cupped the Prophet ﷺ on the crown of his head, so the Prophet ﷺ said to him:

“O Banu Bayadah, marry Abu Hind [to your women], and seek his daughters in marriage.”

And he said: “If there is any good in what you use for treatment, then it is cupping.”

And in one narration: “He was a cupper.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2102), al-Daraqutni (3/300–301), Ibn Hibban (4067), and al-Hakim (2/164).

His statement, “and seek marriage from him,” means: ask for his daughters in marriage.

٦٢١٢ — عن عائشة أنها قالت: كان في بريرة ثلاث سنن: فكانت إحدى السنن الثلاث أنها أعتقت فخيرت في زوجها. وقال رسول الله ﷺ: (( الولاء لمن أعتق )). ودخل رسول الله ﷺ والبرمة تفور بلحم، فقرب إليه خبز وأدم من أدم البيت. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: (( ألم أر البرمة فيها لحم؟ )) فقالوا: بلى يا رسول الله، ولكن لحم تصدق به على بريرة، وأنت لا تأكل الصدقة. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: (( هو عليها صدقة، وهو لنا هدية )).

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٢٩)، والبخاري (٥٢٧٩)، ومسلم (١٤:١٥٠٤).

english_source:
6212 — ‘A’ishah said: There were three legal rulings connected to Barirah. One of those three rulings was that when she was freed, she was given the choice regarding her husband. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The right of patronage belongs to the one who frees.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered while a cooking pot was boiling with meat, and bread and ordinary household seasoning were brought near to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Did I not see the pot with meat in it?” They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah, but it is meat that was given in charity to Barirah, and you do not eat charity. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “For her it is charity, and for us it is a gift.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (29), al-Bukhari (5279), and Muslim (1504:14).

٦٢١٣ — عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ قالت: كان زوج بريرة عبداً، فخيرها رسول الله ﷺ، فاختارت نفسها، ولو كان حراً لم يخيرها.

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٩:١٥٠٤).

english_source:
6213 — ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: The husband of Barirah was a slave, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave her the choice, and she chose herself. If he had been a free man, he would not have given her that choice.

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1504:9).

٦٢١٤ — عن ابن عباس أن زوج بريرة كان عبداً يقال له مغيث، كأني أنظر إليه يطوف خلفها يبكي ودموعه تسيل على لحيته. فقال النبي ﷺ لعباس: (( يا عباس، ألا تعجب من حب مغيث بريرة، ومن بغض بريرة مغيثاً؟ )). فقال النبي ﷺ: (( لو راجعته )). قالت: يا رسول الله، تأمرني؟ قال: (( إنما أنا أشفع )). قالت: لا حاجة لي فيه.

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥٢٨٣).

english_source:
6214 — Ibn ‘Abbas reported that the husband of Barirah was a slave named Mughith. It is as if I can still see him going around behind her, weeping, with tears flowing down his beard. Then the Prophet ﷺ said to al-‘Abbas:

“O ‘Abbas, are you not amazed at the love of Mughith for Barirah, and the dislike of Barirah for Mughith?”

Then the Prophet ﷺ said: “Why do you not return to him?” She said: O Messenger of Allah, are you commanding me? He said: “I am only interceding.” She said: I have no need of him.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5283).

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥٢٨١).

6215 — Ibn ‘Abbas said: That was Mughith, the slave of such-and-such people - meaning the husband of Barirah. It is as though I can still see him following her through the streets of Madinah, weeping over her.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5281).

٦٢١٦ — عن ابن عباس أن زوج بريرة كان عبدا أسود يسمى مُغيثا. قال: فكنت أراه يتبعها في سكك المدينة، يعصر عينيه عليها. قال: وقضى فيها النبي ﷺ أربع قضيات: إن مواليها اشترطوا الولاء، فقضى النبي ﷺ: (( الولاء لمن أعتق )). وخيّرها فاختارت نفسها، فأمرها أن تعتد. قال: وتُصُدِّقَ عليها بصدقة، فأهدت منها إلى عائشة، فذكرت ذلك للنبي ﷺ فقال: (( هو عليها صدقة، وإلينا هدية )).

صحيح: رواه أحمد (٢٥٤٢)، والطبراني (١١٨٢٦)، والبيهقي (٢٢٢-٢٢١/٧).

english_source:
6216 — Ibn ‘Abbas reported that the husband of Barirah was a black slave named Mughith. He said: I used to see him following her through the streets of Madinah, crying over her. He said: The Prophet ﷺ gave four rulings regarding her case: her masters had stipulated that the right of patronage would remain with them, so the Prophet ﷺ ruled, “The right of patronage belongs to the one who frees.” He gave her the choice, and she chose herself. He ordered her to observe her waiting period. And charity was given to her, then she gifted some of it to ‘A’ishah, and when that was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ he said, “For her it is charity, and for us it is a gift.”

Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (2542), al-Tabarani (11826), and al-Bayhaqi (7/221–222).

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5707).

٦٢٢٠ — عن فاطمة بنت قيس تقول: إن زوجها طلّقها ثلاثاً فلم يجعل لها رسول الله ﷺ سكنى ولا نفقة. قالت: قال لي رسول الله ﷺ: (( إذا حللت فآذنيني )). فآذنته. فخطبها معاوية وأبو جهم وأسامة بن زيد، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: (( أما معاوية فرجل ترب لا مال له، وأما أبو جهم فرجل ضرّاب، ولكن أسامة بن زيد )).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٤٧ :١٤٨٠).

english_source:
6220 — Fatimah bint Qays said: Her husband divorced her with a final triple divorce, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not assign for her housing or maintenance. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me, “When your waiting period ends, inform me.” So I informed him. Then Mu‘awiyah, Abu Jahm, and Usamah ibn Zayd proposed to her, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “As for Mu‘awiyah, he is a poor man with no wealth. As for Abu Jahm, he is a man who beats women. But Usamah ibn Zayd…”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1480:47).

٦٢٢٢ — عن مسروق وعمرو بن عتبة أنهما كتبا إلى سبيعة بنت الحارث يسألانها عن أمرها - فكتبت لهما الحديث مطولاً كما سيأتي -، وفي آخره أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: (( إن وجدتِ زوجاً صالحاً فتزوجي )).

صحيح: رواه ابن ماجه (٢٠٢٨).

6222 — Masruq and ‘Amr ibn ‘Utbah wrote to Subay‘ah bint al-Harith asking her about her case - and she wrote back to them the full narration, which will come later - and at its end the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If you find a righteous husband, then marry.”

Authentic: Narrated by Ibn Majah (2028).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٠٨٢)، ومسلم (٢٥٢٧).

6224 — Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ proposed to Umm Hani’ bint Abi Talib. She said: “O Messenger of Allah, I have grown old and I have dependents.” So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “The best women who have ridden camels are the women of Quraysh, the most compassionate toward a child in his young age.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2527:201).

٦٢٢٥ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قيل: يا رسول الله، أي النساء خير؟ قال: (( التي تسره إذا نظر، وتطيعه إذا أمر، ولا تخالفه في نفسها ومالها بما يكره )).

حسن: رواه النسائي (٣٢٣١)، وأحمد (٧٤٢١)، والبيهقي (٨٢/٧).

6225 — Abu Hurayrah said: It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, which women are best?” He said, “The one who pleases him when he looks at her, obeys him when he commands her, and does not oppose him concerning herself or his wealth in a way he dislikes.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Nasa’i (3231), Ahmad (7421), and al-Bayhaqi (7/82).

Hasan: Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu‘jam al-Kabir (14/338, no. 14969).

٦٢٢٧ — عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله ﷺ: (( أيما امرأة تزوجت بغير إذن وليها فنكاحها باطل، فإن دخل بها فلها المهر بما استحل من فرجها، وإن اشتجروا فالسلطان ولي من لا ولي له )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٠٨٣)، والترمذي (١١٠٢)، وابن ماجه (١٨٧٩)، وصححه ابن حبان (٤٠٧٤).

english_source:
6227 — ‘A’ishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Any woman who marries without the permission of her guardian, then her marriage is invalid. If he has consummated the marriage with her, then she is entitled to the dowry because he made her private part lawful for himself. And if they dispute, then the ruler is the guardian of the one who has no guardian.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2083), al-Tirmidhi (1102), Ibn Majah (1879), and authenticated by Ibn Hibban (4074).

٦٢٣٢ — عن سالم بن عبد الله أنه سمع عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما يحدث: (( إن عمر بن الخطاب حين تأيمت حفصة بنت عمر من خنيس بن حذافة السهمي - وكان من أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ فتوفي بالمدينة - فقال عمر بن الخطاب: أتيت عثمان بن عفان فعرضت عليه حفصة، فقال: سأنظر في أمري. فلبثت ليالي ثم لقيني فقال: قد بدا لي أن لا أتزوج يومي هذا. قال عمر: فلقيت أبا بكر الصديق فقلت: إن شئت زوجتك حفصة بنت عمر، فصمت أبو بكر فلم يرجع إلي شيئا، وكنت أوجد عليه مني على عثمان، فلبثت ليالي ثم خطبها رسول الله ﷺ فأنكحتها إياه، فلقيني أبو بكر فقال: لعلك وجدت علي حين عرضت علي حفصة فلم أرجع إليك شيئا؟ قال عمر: قلت نعم. قال أبو بكر: فإنه لم يمنعني أن أرجع إليك فيما عرضت علي إلا أني كنت علمت أن رسول الله ﷺ قد ذكرها، فلم أكن لأفشي سر رسول الله ﷺ، ولو تركها رسول الله ﷺ قبلتها ))

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥١٢٢).

6232 — Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah reported that he heard ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar narrating: When Hafsah bint ‘Umar became widowed after Khunays ibn Hudhafah al-Sahmi - who had been one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and had died in Madinah - ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab said: I went to ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan and offered Hafsah to him, and he said: “I will consider my matter.” A few nights passed, then he met me and said: “It seems to me that I should not marry at this time.”

‘Umar said: Then I met Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and said: “If you wish, I will marry Hafsah bint ‘Umar to you.” Abu Bakr remained silent and gave me no reply, and I was more upset with him than with ‘Uthman. Then a few nights passed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed to her, so I married her to him. Then Abu Bakr met me and said: “Perhaps you were upset with me when you offered Hafsah to me and I gave you no response?” ‘Umar said: I said, “Yes.” Abu Bakr said: “Nothing prevented me from replying to you except that I knew the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had mentioned her, and I would never disclose the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Had the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left her, I would have accepted her.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5122).

٦٢٣٣ — عن أم حبيبة بنت أبي سفيان، قالت: دخل علي رسول الله ﷺ فقلت له: هل لك في أختي بنت أبي سفيان؟ فقال: (( أفعل ماذا؟ )) قلت: تنكحها. قال: (( أوتحبين ذلك؟ )) قلت: لست لك بمخلية، وأحب من شركني في الخير أختي … الحديث.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥١٠١)، ومسلم (١٥ :١٤٤٩)، واللفظ لمسلم.

قولها: (( لست لك بمخلية )) أي لست بمنفردة بك ولا خالية من ضرة.

6233 — Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon me, and I said to him, “Would you like my sister, the daughter of Abu Sufyan?” He said, “What would I do?” I said, “Marry her.” He said, “Would you like that?” I said, “I am not the only one for you, and the one I would most love to share in good with me is my sister…”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5101) and Muslim (1449:15), and this wording is that of Muslim.

Her saying, “I am not the only one for you,” means: I am not alone with you and not free from having a co-wife.

٦٢٣٤ — عن سهل بن سعد أن امرأة عرضت نفسها على النبي ﷺ فقال له رجل: يا رسول الله، زوجنيها. فقال: (( ما عندك؟ )) فقال: ما عندي شيء. قال: (( اذهب فالتمس ولو خاتماً من حديد )). فذهب ثم رجع فقال: لا والله ما وجدت شيئاً ولا خاتماً من حديد، ولكن هذا إزاري ولها نصفه. قال سهل: وماله رداء. فقال النبي ﷺ: (( وما تصنع بإزارك؟ إن لبسته لم يكن عليها منه شيء، وإن لبسته لم يكن عليك منه شيء )). فجلس الرجل حتى إذا طال مجلسه قام، فرآه النبي ﷺ فدعاه - أو دعي له - فقال له: (( ماذا معك من القرآن؟ )) فقال: معي سورة كذا وسورة كذا - لسور يعددها - فقال النبي ﷺ: (( أملكناكها بما معك من القرآن )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥١٢١)، ومسلم (١٤٢٥). واللفظ للبخاري.

٦٢٣٥ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: جاءت امرأة إلى رسول الله ﷺ تعرض عليه نفسها، قالت: يا رسول الله، ألك بي حاجة؟ فقالت بنت أنس: ما أقل حياءها، واسوأتاه. قال: هي خير منك، رغبت في النبي ﷺ فعرضت عليه نفسها.

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥١٢٠).

6235 — Anas ibn Malik said: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ offering herself to him. She said, “O Messenger of Allah, do you have any need of me?” The daughter of Anas said, “How little modesty she had! What a shame!” He said: She was better than you; she desired the Prophet ﷺ, so she offered herself to him.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5120).

٦٢٣٦ — عن عائشة قالت: كنت أغار على اللاتي وهبن أنفسهن لرسول الله ﷺ، وأقول: أتهب المرأة نفسها؟ فلما نزل قوله تعالى: (تُرْجِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ وَتُؤْوِي إِلَيْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَمَنِ ابْتَغَيْتَ مِمَّنْ عَزَلْتَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكَ) [الأحزاب: ٥١] قالت: قلت: والله ما أرى ربك إلا يسارع لك في هواك.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٧٨٨)، ومسلم (١٤٦٣).

english_source:
6236 — ‘A’ishah said: I used to feel jealous of those women who offered themselves to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I would say, “Does a woman offer herself?” Then when the saying of Allah Most High was revealed:

“You may defer whom you will of them and take to yourself whom you will, and whomever you desire of those you had set aside - there is no blame upon you.” [Al-Ahzab: 51]

she said: I said, “By Allah, I see that your Lord hastens to fulfill what pleases you.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (4788) and Muslim (1463).

٦٢٣٧ — عن عروة قال:

كانت خولة بنت حكيم من اللائي وهبن أنفسهن للنبي ﷺ.

فقالت عائشة:

أما تستحي المرأة أن تهب نفسها للرجل؟

فلما نزلت:

﴿تُرْجِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ﴾

 [الأحزاب: ٥١]

قلت:

يا رسول الله، ما أرى ربك إلا يسارع في هواك.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥١١٣)، ومسلم (١٤٦٤/٥٠). 

وقوله: ﴿تُرْجِي﴾ أي تؤخر من تشاء من الواهبات.

وقوله: ﴿وَتُؤْوِي﴾ أي تقبل من شئت من الواهبات، ورددت من شئت، ثم من رددتها فأنت فيها أيضًا بالخيار بعد ذلك، إن شئت عدت فيها فآويتها.

قولها: «هواك» أي رضاك، ولكن الغيرة جعلتها تقول: هواك؛ لأن إضافة الهوى إلى النبي ﷺ لا تحمل على ظاهرها، لأنه لا ينطق عن الهوى، ولا يفعل بالهوى.

6237 — ʿUrwah reported:

Khawlah bint Ḥakīm was among the women who offered themselves in marriage to the Prophet ﷺ.

ʿĀʾishah said:

“Does a woman not feel shy to offer herself to a man?”

Then when the verse was revealed:

“You may defer whom you wish of them…”

 [al-Aḥzāb: 51]

I said:

“O Messenger of Allah, I see that your Lord hastens to fulfill what pleases you.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5113) and Muslim (1464/50). 

The word “turjī” means: you may defer whichever of the women who offered themselves you wish.

“And you may take in” means: you may accept whichever of them you wish and put aside whichever you wish; and even one whom you previously put aside remains subject to your choice afterward—if you wish, you may return to her and accept her.

Her expression “what you desire” means what pleases you. Jealousy caused her to phrase it in that manner; attributing mere personal whim to the Prophet ﷺ is not intended literally, because he does not speak from whim nor act from whim.

Then when the verse was revealed:

“You may defer whom you wish of them…”

 [al-Aḥzāb: 51]

I said:

“O Messenger of Allah, I see that your Lord hastens to fulfill what pleases you.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5113) and Muslim (1464/50). 

The word “turjī” means: you may defer whichever of the women who offered themselves you wish.

“And you may take in” means: you may accept whichever of them you wish and put aside whichever you wish; and even one whom you previously put aside remains subject to your choice afterward—if you wish, you may return to her and accept her.

Her expression “what you desire” means what pleases you. Jealousy caused her to phrase it in that manner; attributing mere personal whim to the Prophet ﷺ is not intended literally, because he does not speak from whim nor act from whim.

٦٢٣٧ — عن عروة قال:

كانت خولة بنت حكيم من اللائي وهبن أنفسهن للنبي ﷺ.

فقالت عائشة:

أما تستحي المرأة أن تهب نفسها للرجل؟

فلما نزلت:

﴿تُرْجِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ﴾

 [الأحزاب: ٥١]

قلت:

يا رسول الله، ما أرى ربك إلا يسارع في هواك.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥١١٣)، ومسلم (١٤٦٤/٥٠). 

وقوله: ﴿تُرْجِي﴾ أي تؤخر من تشاء من الواهبات.

وقوله: ﴿وَتُؤْوِي﴾ أي تقبل من شئت من الواهبات، ورددت من شئت، ثم من رددتها فأنت فيها أيضًا بالخيار بعد ذلك، إن شئت عدت فيها فآويتها.

قولها: «هواك» أي رضاك، ولكن الغيرة جعلتها تقول: هواك؛ لأن إضافة الهوى إلى النبي ﷺ لا تحمل على ظاهرها، لأنه لا ينطق عن الهوى، ولا يفعل بالهوى.

Khawlah bint Ḥakīm was among the women who offered themselves in marriage to the Prophet ﷺ.

ʿĀʾishah said:

“Does a woman not feel shy to offer herself to a man?”

Then when the verse was revealed:

“You may defer whom you wish of them…”

 [al-Aḥzāb: 51]

I said:

“O Messenger of Allah, I see that your Lord hastens to fulfill what pleases you.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5113) and Muslim (1464/50).

“And you may take in” means: you may accept whichever of them you wish and put aside whichever you wish; and even one whom you previously put aside remains subject to your choice afterward—if you wish, you may return to her and accept her.

Her expression “what you desire” means what pleases you. Jealousy caused her to phrase it in that manner; attributing mere personal whim to the Prophet ﷺ is not intended literally, because he does not speak from whim nor act from whim.

٦٢٣٩ — عن عائشة قالت: تزوجني رسول الله ﷺ وأنا بنت ست سنين، وبنى بي وأنا بنت تسع سنين، قالت: فقدمنا المدينة، فنزلنا في بني الحارث بن خزرج، فوعكت فتمزق شعري، فوفى جميمة، فأتتني أمي أم رومان، وأنا على أرجوحة، ومعي صواحبي، فصرخت بي فأتيتها، لا أدري ما تريد بي، فأخذت بيدي حتى أوقفتني على الباب. فقلت: هه هه، حتى ذهب نفسي فأدخلتني بيتا، فإذا نسوة من الأنصار، فقلن: على الخير والبركة، وعلى خير طائر، فأسلمتني إليهن، فغسلن رأسي وأصلحنني، فلم يرعني إلا رسول الله ﷺ ضحى. فأسلمتني إليه.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٨٩٤) ومسلم (١٤٢٢).

وقولها: "جميمة" تصغير جمة وهي الشعر النازل إلى الأذنين ونحوهما أي صار إلى هذا الحد بعد أن كان

قد ذهب بالمرض.

english_source:
6239 — ʿAʾishah reported: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married me when I was six years old and consummated the marriage with me when I was nine years old. We then came to Madinah and stayed among Banu al-Harith ibn Khazraj. I fell ill and my hair fell out, then it grew back to around ear-length. My mother, Umm Ruman, came to me while I was on a swing with some girl companions. She called me, so I went to her without knowing what she wanted. She took me by the hand until she made me stand at the door. I said, ‘Hah, hah,’ until my breath settled, then she brought me into a house. There were women from the Ansar inside, and they said: ‘With goodness and blessing, and with good fortune.’ She handed me over to them, and they washed my head and prepared me. Nothing startled me except the Messenger of Allah ﷺ coming in the forenoon. Then she handed me over to him.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3894) and Muslim (1422).

Her saying, “Jamima,” is the diminutive of “jamma,” which refers to hair that falls to the ears and the like—meaning it had grown to this length after having

fallen out due to illness.

٦٢٤١ — عن أبي سلمة ويحيى قالا: لما هلكت خديجة، جاءت خولة بنت حكيم امرأة عثمان ابن مظعون قالت: يا رسول الله، ألا تزوج؟ قال: (( من؟ )) قالت: إن شئت بكراً، وإن شئت ثيّباً، قال: (( فمن البكر؟ )) قالت: ابنة أحب خلق الله عز وجل إليك: عائشة بنت أبي بكر. قال: (( ومن الثيب؟ )) قالت: سودة بنت زمعة، آمنت بك واتبعتك على ما تقول، قال: (( فاذهبي فاذكريهما عليَّ)).

فدخلت بيت أبي بكر، فقالت: يا أم رومان، ماذا أدخل الله عز وجل عليكم من الخير والبركة؟ قالت: وما ذاك؟ قالت: أرسلني رسول الله ﷺ أخطب عليه عائشة، قالت: انتظري أبا بكر حتى يأتي، فجاء أبو بكر، فقالت: يا أبا بكر، ماذا أدخل الله عز وجل عليكم من الخير والبركة؟ قال: وما ذاك؟ قالت: أرسلني رسول الله ﷺ أخطب عليه عائشة. قال: وهل تصلح له، إنما هي ابنة أخيه، فرجعت إلى رسول الله ﷺ فذكرت ذلك له. قال: (( ارجعي إليه فقولي له: أنا أخوك وأنت أخي في الإسلام، وابنتك تصلح لي)).

فرجعت، فذكرتْ ذلك له. قال: انتظري، وخرج. قالت أم رومان: إن مُطْعِم بن عدي قد كان ذكرها على ابنه، فوالله ما وعد وعداً قط فأخلفه لأبي بكر، فدخل أبو بكر على مطعم بن عدي، وعنده امرأته أم الفتى، فقالت: يا ابن أبي قحافة، لعلك مُصْبِئٌ صاحبنا، مُدْخِله في دينك الذي أنت عليه، إن تزوج إليك. قال أبو بكر للمطعم بن عدي: أقول هذه تقول؟ قال: إنها تقول ذلك، فخرج من عنده، وقد أذهب الله عز وجل ما كان في نفسه من عِدَته التي وعده، فرجع، فقال لخولة: ادعي لي رسول الله ﷺ، فدعته، فزوجها إياه، وعائشة يومئذ بنت ست سنين.

ثم خرجت، فدخلت على سودة بنت زمعة، فقالت: ماذا أدخل الله عز وجل عليك من الخير والبركة؟ قالت: وما ذاك؟ قالت: أرسلني رسول الله ﷺ أخطبك عليه. قالت: وددت، ادخلي إلى أبي، فاذكري ذاك له، وكان شيخاً كبيراً قد أدركته السن، قد تخلَّف عن الحج، فدخلت عليه، فحيته بتحية الجاهلية، فقال: من هذه؟ فقالت: خولة بنت حكيم، قال: فما شأنك؟ قالت: أرسلني محمد بن عبد الله، أخطب عليه سودة، قال: كفء كريم، ماذا تقول صاحبتك؟ قالت: تحب ذاك، قال: ادعها لي، فدعتها.

فقال: أي بنية، إن هذه تزعم أن محمد بن عبد الله بن عبد المطلب قد أرسل يخطبك وهو كفء كريم، أتحبين أن أزوجك به؟ قالت: نعم، قال: ادعيه لي، فجاء رسول الله ﷺ إليه، فزوّجها إياه، فجاءها أخوها عبد بن زمعة من الحج، فجعل يحثي على رأسه التراب، فقال بعد أن أسلم: لعمرك، إني لسفيه يوم أحثي في رأسي التراب أن تزوّج رسول الله ﷺ سودة بنت زمعة.

قالت عائشة: فقدمنا المدينة، فنزلنا في بني الحارث من الخزرج في السُّنْح، قالت: فجاء رسول الله ﷺ فدخل بيتنا، واجتمع إليه رجال من الأنصار ونساء، فجاءت بي أمي، وإني لفي أرجوحة بين عَذْقين ترجح بي، فأنزلتني من الأرجوحة، ولي جُميمة، ففرقتها، ومسحت وجهي بشيء من ماء، ثم أقبلت تقودني حتى وقفت بي عند الباب، وإني لأنهج، حتى سكن من نفسي، ثم دخلت بي، فإذا رسول الله ﷺ جالس على سرير في بيتنا، وعنده رجال ونساء من الأنصار، فأجلستني في حِجْره، ثم قالت: هؤلاء أهلك، فبارك الله لك فيهم، وبارك لهم فيك، فوثب الرجال والنساء، فخرجوا، وبنى بي رسول الله ﷺ في بيتنا، ما نُحِرت عليَّ جزور، ولا ذُبِحت عليَّ شاة، حتى أرسل إلينا سعد بن عبادة بجفنة كان يرسل بها إلى رسول الله ﷺ إذا دار إلى نسائه، وأنا يومئذ بنت تسع سنين.

6241 — Abu Salamah and Yahya said: When Khadijah died, Khawlah bint Hakim, the wife of ‘Uthman ibn Maz‘un, came and said: O Messenger of Allah, will you not marry? He said, “Whom?” She said: If you wish, a virgin; and if you wish, a previously married woman. He said, “Who is the virgin?” She said: The daughter of the most beloved of Allah’s creation to you: ‘A’ishah daughter of Abu Bakr. He said, “And who is the previously married woman?” She said: Sawdah bint Zam‘ah. She believed in you and followed what you brought. He said, “Go and mention them to me.”

So she entered the house of Abu Bakr and said: O Umm Ruman, what goodness and blessing Allah has brought to your household. She said: And what is that? She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has sent me to ask for ‘A’ishah in marriage for him. She said: Wait until Abu Bakr comes. When Abu Bakr came, she said: O Abu Bakr, what goodness and blessing Allah has brought to your household. He said: And what is that? She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has sent me to ask for ‘A’ishah in marriage for him. He said: Is she suitable for him? She is the daughter of his brother. So she returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him. He said: “Go back to him and say: I am your brother and you are my brother in Islam, and your daughter is lawful for me.”

So she went back and mentioned that to him. He said: Wait. Then he went out. Umm Ruman said: Mut‘im ibn ‘Adi had already mentioned her for his son, and by Allah he had never made a promise to Abu Bakr and broken it. So Abu Bakr went to Mut‘im ibn ‘Adi, and with him was the boy’s mother. She said: O son of Abu Quhafah, perhaps you will turn our companion away from his religion and enter him into your religion if he marries into you. Abu Bakr said to Mut‘im ibn ‘Adi: Is this what she is saying? He said: She is saying that. So he left him, and Allah removed from his heart the matter of the promise he had made to him. Then he returned and said to Khawlah: Call the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for me. So she called him, and he married her to him, and ‘A’ishah was then six years old.

Then she went out and entered upon Sawdah bint Zam‘ah and said: What goodness and blessing Allah has brought to you. She said: And what is that? She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has sent me to ask for you in marriage for him. She said: I would like that. Go in to my father and mention it to him. He was a very old man who had advanced in age and had stayed behind from Hajj. She entered upon him and greeted him with the greeting of the pre-Islamic period. He said: Who is this? She said: Khawlah bint Hakim. He said: What is your matter? She said: Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah has sent me; he is asking for Sawdah in marriage. He said: A noble and suitable match. What does your companion say? She said: She would like that. He said: Call her for me. So she called her.

He said: My daughter, this woman claims that Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib has sent to ask for your hand, and he is a noble and suitable match. Do you wish that I marry you to him? She said: Yes. He said: Call him for me. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and he married her to him. Then her brother ‘Abd ibn Zam‘ah came back from Hajj and began throwing dust upon his own head. After he accepted Islam, he said: By your life, I was indeed foolish on the day I threw dust on my head because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Sawdah bint Zam‘ah.

‘A’ishah said: Then we came to Madinah and stayed among Banu al-Harith of al-Khazraj at al-Sunh. She said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and entered our house, and men and women from the Ansar gathered there. My mother came to me while I was on a swing between two branches, swinging on it. She brought me down from the swing, and my hair had grown to around ear-length. She combed and arranged it and wiped my face with some water. Then she came leading me until she made me stand at the door while I was breathing heavily, until I calmed down. Then she took me in, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seated on a bed in our house, with men and women from the Ansar around him. She seated me in his lap, then said: These are your family. May Allah bless you in them, and bless them through you. Then the men and women stood up and left. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ consummated the marriage with me in our house. No camel was slaughtered for me and no sheep was slaughtered for me, until Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah sent us a large bowl which he used to send to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whenever he was with one of his wives. I was nine years old at that time.

Hasan: Narrated by Imam Ahmad (25769).

She said: O son of Abu Quhafah, perhaps you will turn our companion away from his religion and enter him into your religion if he marries into you. Abu Bakr said to Mut‘im ibn ‘Adi: Is this what she is saying? He said: She is saying that. So he left him, and Allah removed from his heart the matter of the promise he had made to him. Then he returned and said to Khawlah: Call the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for me. So she called him, and he married her to him, and ‘A’ishah was then six years old.

Then she went out and entered upon Sawdah bint Zam‘ah and said: What goodness and blessing Allah has brought to you. She said: And what is that? She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has sent me to ask for you in marriage for him. She said: I would like that. Go in to my father and mention it to him. He was a very old man who had advanced in age and had stayed behind from Hajj. She entered upon him and greeted him with the greeting of the pre-Islamic period. He said: Who is this? She said: Khawlah bint Hakim. He said: What is your matter? She said: Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah has sent me; he is asking for Sawdah in marriage. He said: A noble and suitable match. What does your companion say? She said: She would like that. He said: Call her for me. So she called her.

He said: My daughter, this woman claims that Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib has sent to ask for your hand, and he is a noble and suitable match. Do you wish that I marry you to him? She said: Yes. He said: Call him for me. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and he married her to him. Then her brother ‘Abd ibn Zam‘ah came back from Hajj and began throwing dust upon his own head. After he accepted Islam, he said: By your life, I was indeed foolish on the day I threw dust on my head because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Sawdah bint Zam‘ah.

‘A’ishah said: Then we came to Madinah and stayed among Banu al-Harith of al-Khazraj at al-Sunh. She said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and entered our house, and men and women from the Ansar gathered there. My mother came to me while I was on a swing between two branches, swinging on it. She brought me down from the swing, and my hair had grown to around ear-length. She combed and arranged it and wiped my face with some water. Then she came leading me until she made me stand at the door while I was breathing heavily, until I calmed down. Then she took me in, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seated on a bed in our house, with men and women from the Ansar around him. She seated me in his lap, then said: These are your family. May Allah bless you in them, and bless them through you. Then the men and women stood up and left. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ consummated the marriage with me in our house. No camel was slaughtered for me and no sheep was slaughtered for me, until Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah sent us a large bowl which he used to send to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whenever he was with one of his wives. I was nine years old at that time.

Hasan: Narrated by Imam Ahmad (25769).
